<a id="add-family-connector"></a>

### Add family connector

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-26 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** put a duct, pipe or electrical connector on this face of the family - or on a flange ring's face, sized by its opening - sized by its parameters.

Puts one MEP CONNECTOR on a face of the family open in the Family Editor - the face lying on a named reference plane, "Neck Top" - for the system named, and ties its size to the family's own parameters: a rectangular duct port to Neck Width and Neck Depth, a round duct or a pipe to one diameter. The connector sits at the centre of that face and points out of it. **A NEW CONNECTOR DOES NOT TAKE ITS FACE'S SIZE.** It comes out at a generic one foot, whatever face it is on - reported from an earlier family build, on a 200 x 200 face and again on a 45 mm pipe stub. So a duct or pipe connector is refused without the parameters that size it, and those are ASSOCIATED to the connector's own width, height or diameter - so the port follows the neck when the family is resized, instead of being right once. An electrical connector has no size and takes none. **CABLE TRAY AND CONDUIT** (version 4, 2026-10-13, the gap fill): a tray port sized by width then height, a conduit port by its diameter. **THE FACE IS NAMED BY THE PLANE IT LIES ON.** A face cannot be typed, but every face of a box built by EXTRUDE_BETWEEN_PLANES lies on a named plane. Exactly one solid face must lie on the plane named; none, or more than one, is refused with the count, because a connector on the wrong face points the wrong way and nothing about it looks wrong in plan. **ONLY A FACE THAT FACES OUT, AT THE POINT GIVEN (version 7, issue #1029).** A plane is infinite, so on a real family more than one face lies on it - in the issue's pump, the raised face's top and four lid screws a metre away at the same height, and on the plane below, the flange top and the raised face's own underside. A face that faces into another solid all over is inside the body and never counts: it is left out and said. `at`, the connector's centre in mm, leaves out every face whose centre is not within 1 mm of it; `form` and `facing` narrow it the same way. And where the face chosen is covered at its own centre on the side it points - the flange top under its raised face - nothing is made and the form covering it is named, because a connector there would sit inside that form. **A JOINED OR CUT FORM'S FACE IS FOUND TOO (version 3, row 5b-410).** Once a form is joined or cut by COMBINE_FAMILY_FORMS - a flange cut by a bore void - Revit keeps its faces in the combination's geometry and the form's own reads empty, so a flange face exactly on its plane came back "no solid face". Every combination's faces are now searched when no form's own face lies on the plane, under the same rule: exactly one, or refused with the count. A form's own face is still used first, so a thin solid joined to nothing, laid on a cut face, takes the connector wherever Revit will not take it on the joined face - and where a form's own face wins with joined faces on the same plane too, the result says how many. What Revit's reference to a joined face names, and whether Revit takes a connector on it, is reported as Revit answers; a refusal names that way round. **THE SYSTEM DECIDES THE KIND.** "Supply Air" makes a duct connector, "Domestic Cold Water" a pipe one, "Power Balanced" an electrical one - matched to Revit's own system names, spaces ignored, never guessed. The name Revit's System Classification list shows is taken too where it differs from the API's - "Fire Protection Wet", "Fire Protection Pre-Action", "Hydronic Supply" - so what the modeller reads in Revit is what they can type (row 5b-297). A bare "Other" is not taken: a duct has Other Air and a pipe Other Pipe. Revit has no steam system; a steam connection is Other Pipe. **GLOBAL AND FITTING ARE TAKEN TOO** - a valve body's two connectors are Global so a system passes through it. Both are a duct and a pipe system, so the domain comes from the words, "Global pipe", or else from the family's category: Global on a Pipe Accessories family is a pipe connector. Where Revit refuses one, its words are reported and nothing is kept. **WHICH WAY ROUND IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED.** Revit takes a connector's own width direction from the face, not from the family's X, so a parameter named "Neck Width" can come out driving the port's height. The face is measured along the connector's own axes and the two parameters are tied the way round the face is built - a 400 x 300 neck gets a 400 x 300 port - and the report says when they were turned. Parameters that fit the face neither way round are refused: that port would not fit the face it sits on. **DUCT SIZE AND PIPE SIZE PARAMETERS SIZE IT TOO (version 8, row 5b-2031).** A shared parameter of spec Duct Size sizes a duct connector's width and height, and one of spec Pipe Size a pipe connector's diameter, as Revit's own Associate Family Parameter allows; a Length parameter sizes any connector. A Duct Size parameter given for a pipe connector, or the other way, is refused by name. **IN A RING'S OPENING, A PORT UP TO ITS SIZE (version 8, row 5b-2032).** A flange is bored a little over its duct - a 205 x 205 duct in a 209 x 209 opening - so on a ring face the port must fit INSIDE the opening, centred, either way round, and the answer says the clearance each side. On a whole face the face is the port, and it is still matched exactly. A port larger than the opening is refused. **THE SIZE IS READ BACK, AND A MISMATCH IS NOT KEPT.** After the ties the connector's width and height are read against the face, or its diameter against its parameter; one that differs fails the call. Flow direction, description and electrical load are left at Revit's defaults; SET_FAMILY_CONNECTOR_ROLES changes them, and the system, afterwards. **ALL OR NOTHING.** A connector that cannot be tied to its size is not left behind at one foot: the call fails and nothing is kept. **A FLANGE RING'S FACE IS MEASURED BY ITS OPENING (version 5, 2026-10-24, row 5b-1334).** A duct accessory's port belongs on its flange: a ring round the duct opening, 600 x 400 inside and 640 x 440 outside. Version 4 measured the whole outline and refused the ring - "a port sized by them would not fit the face it sits on". Now, when one inner loop of the face holds the connector's centre, that loop - the opening - is measured, and the connector must sit at its centre or nothing is kept; a face of one loop is measured whole, exactly as before. Two openings round the centre are refused. Measured first on Revit 2020 (rolled back, in the owner's volume control damper): a ring sketched on the end plane took the connector at its centre and moved with that plane when Length changed. A REFERENCE PLANE ALONE TAKES NO CONNECTOR through the API - "oEdgeLoopRef.ptr() is NULL", and a sketch plane made from it "is not a planar face" - and a nested family's face took one off-centre that stayed put when the frame moved; the ring is the way round both. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="add-family-flip-control"></a>

### Add family flip control

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-03 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** add flip arrows to the family being edited, so a placed copy flips left-right or front-back in one click.

Adds FLIP CONTROLS to the family open in the Family Editor - the small arrows a placed door, window, fan coil or valve shows when selected, which turn or mirror it in one click instead of a mirror that moves it. The Family Editor's Control tool. **FOUR SHAPES, AS THE CONTROL TOOL NAMES THEM** - single horizontal, double horizontal, single vertical, double vertical - each placed in a FLOOR PLAN or CEILING PLAN of the family, the only views Revit's NewControl takes, at a point in millimetres in the plan's own X,Y. Several at once, `|` between. Where a floor plan and a ceiling plan share the name, the floor plan is taken - whether a template's "Ref. Level" is both is what BV1's view list shows. **WHAT EACH DOES TO A PLACED COPY IS REVIT'S.** Autodesk's remark on Control, 2020 to 2027: a single arrow, horizontal or vertical, ROTATES the copy 180 degrees; a double arrow MIRRORS it - horizontally or vertically. NEEDS- CHECKING BV3 records what a placed copy does. **READ BACK, ALL OR NOTHING**: every control's shape, view and position are read again; one that does not read as asked fails the call. Their ids come back. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="add-family-model-text"></a>

### Add family model text

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-26 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** place 3D model text - a raised or engraved label, a nameplate - on a named plane in the family being edited.

Places MODEL TEXT in the family open in the Family Editor - the Family Editor's Model Text button, typed rather than clicked: a nameplate on a panel, a raised or engraved label, a legend. Real 3D lettering that shows in 3D and elevation and stays editable as text afterwards. One or many texts in one call, ONE entry in the undo list. **EACH ROW STARTS `text=`** and gives `workPlane` (a reference plane or level by name - "Center (Front/Back)", "Ref. Level"), `at` (where), `heightMm` (the letters' height) and `depthMm` (how far they stand out). Optional: `align` (left, center, right - left is Revit's own default), `readFrom`, `offsetMm`, `material`, `detailLevels` and `views`. A text holding "=" goes in double quotes. A long list may be a file under %TEMP%\heron-work, its full path given instead, read as CREATE_FAMILY_FORMS reads its file. **`at` IS IN THE PLANE'S OWN TWO MODEL COORDINATES, MILLIMETRES FROM THE FAMILY ORIGIN**, the way the form tools write a profile: on a level or a horizontal plane X,Y as seen in plan; on a plane facing front or back - Center (Front/Back) - X,Z; on a plane facing left or right - Center (Left/Right) - Y,Z. Never relative to the plane and never mirrored by the way it faces. `offsetMm` moves the text off the plane along the axis it faces, positive up (+Z), back (+Y) or right (+X) - onto a box's front face with no plane of its own there. **`readFrom` IS THE SIDE THE TEXT READS CORRECTLY FROM** - top or bottom on a horizontal plane, front or back on a front-back one, left or right on a left-right one; by default top, front and right, the Family Editor's own views. The text stays on the named plane itself when that plane's own axes already read from that side and no offset is given; otherwise it is put on a work plane of its own at the same place, which does NOT follow the named plane when it moves, and the answer says so. **THE HEIGHT IS A TYPE.** A Model Text type of exactly that size is used when the family has one; otherwise the first type by name is copied as "<height> mm" - "40 mm", "2.5 mm" - keeping its font. A family holding no Model Text type at all is refused. **WHERE THE LETTERS LAND IS MEASURED.** Once placed, each text's left end, centre or right end (by `align`) is measured against `at` along the text, its foot against the baseline and its back against the plane plus `offsetMm`. Revit 2020 put an offset text at twice its offset and started a centred one at `at`, so a text that missed by more than half a millimetre is placed again moved by the miss, and the answer says so; one that still misses refuses the whole call, naming where it was asked and where it reached. **MEASURED ON THE LETTERS THEMSELVES (version 3, row 5b-2033).** Where the letters land, how far they reach and how deep they are come from the letters' own solids, not Revit's bounding box for the text - on Revit 2020 the box of a text on a plane away from the origin reached about twice the plane's distance while the text's Depth read as asked. Letters whose solids are not the depth asked keep nothing of the list; where only the box disagrees, the answer says the box is not the letters. With no solid to measure the box is used and the answer says so. **ALL OR NOTHING, READ BACK.** Every row is checked before anything is placed. Each text is read back - its words, type and size, depth, alignment, any material or visibility - with where its letters reach on all three axes and which way it runs; one that reads back wrong keeps nothing of the whole list. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="add-family-parameters"></a>

### Add family parameters

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** add these family parameters to the family being edited - or the office's shared parameters from its shared parameter file - switch existing ones to type or instance, rename them, or replace them with shared ones.

Adds one or more FAMILY parameters to the family open in the Family Editor - Width, Depth, Neck Width - all of one kind (a length, a number, a yes/no...), all type or all instance, filed under one group of the Properties palette. The Family Types dialog's "New Parameter", several at a time. **IT MAKES THE PARAMETERS AND WRITES NO VALUE.** A new length reads zero in every type. Filling them in is SET_FAMILY_TYPE_VALUES, and the ORDER MATTERS: values go in before any dimension is labelled with them, because a label on a parameter that reads zero drives the planes it measures to zero and collapses the family - reported from an earlier family build, and the reason LABEL_FAMILY_DIMENSION refuses a label whose parameter disagrees with the planes. **A NAME ALREADY IN THE FAMILY AS THE SAME PARAMETER IS LEFT ALONE AND NAMED.** Re-running the same request adds nothing twice. When the one already there is a different kind or scope from what was asked, or a shared one, it is a different parameter under a familiar name, and since version 4 the whole call is refused - nothing added - rather than carrying on beside it. This includes the category's own built-in parameters: an Air Terminal already has its flow fields. **THE KIND, THE SCOPE AND THE GROUP ARE ASKED FOR.** Type or instance is a decision about the family - sizes that describe the product are type, anything that varies per placed unit is instance - and it is not guessed. The group is the heading in the Properties palette, matched by the name Revit shows. Left empty for a family kind, lengths and angles go under Dimensions and everything else under Data. **For the office's shared parameters it is never defaulted** - an empty group adding them is refused, nothing added - because where a shared parameter sits is the office's convention, and its kind comes from the file, so no one heading follows from what was asked. Replacing, empty keeps each parameter under its own heading. **ALL OR NOTHING.** Every name, the kind and the group are checked before the first parameter is added. If Revit then refuses one - a character it does not allow in a name - the call fails and nothing from it is kept, rather than half the list being added and the rest reported. **SHARED PARAMETERS TOO (version 4, 2026-11-01).** ADD_FAMILY_SHARED_PARAMETERS was merged into this card and is DEPRECATED. `kind` shared adds the office's shared parameters, from the shared parameter file Revit is set to, which is only read: the kind comes from the file, the GUID is the file's, and a project can then schedule and tag the family's value. `replaceExisting` turns family parameters into shared ones in place - "Width=Unit_Width" - every label, formula, association and value kept. `createMissing` writes a definition the file does not have yet, "Group: Name [Data type]", before adding or replacing it - outside the model, so Undo does not take it back: **this card is ADMIN**, and every call of it needs the Admin switch. **A name already in the family as a DIFFERENT parameter refuses the whole call**, for every kind - the safer of the two cards' rules. **SWITCHING TYPE AND INSTANCE (version 2).** With switchExisting true the names are parameters the family already has - or `all` - and instance says which way they go, several at once. The order is worked out for them, a switch Revit would not allow is refused by name before anything changes, and each is read back, all or nothing. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="add-family-type-parameter"></a>

### Add family type parameter

**DRAFT - not yet usable in a chat - refused until proved (D-117).**

**What it does:** make a Family Type parameter so each type of this family chooses which type of a nested part, or which loaded profile, it uses.

Makes a FAMILY TYPE parameter in the family open in the Family Editor - the Family Types dialog's "Family Type" kind - and links nested parts to it, so each type of this family chooses WHICH TYPE of the nested part it uses: the 5 kW or the 7 kW motor, the lever or the wheel handle, the round or the square profile a sweep is drawn with. **ONE CATEGORY**: only a family of that category already loaded into this one can be its value, which is Revit's rule - a category with nothing loaded is refused, naming LOAD_FAMILY. **IN THE ORDER THAT KEEPS THE GEOMETRY STILL**: the parameter is made, its value in the current type is set to the type the parts already show, and only then are the parts linked - the Label in their Properties. Revit's remarks do not say which of a nested copy's parameters carries that link, so each candidate is offered to Revit's own "can it be linked" test and the one it takes is reported. Then each family type named takes its nested type, chosen only from Revit's own list of what the parameter can hold. **A PARAMETER OF THAT NAME ALREADY HERE IS USED AGAIN ONLY WHEN NOTHING IT DRIVES MOVES**: it must be a Family Type parameter that takes the type the named parts show, and where it already drives parts it must already hold that type - otherwise setting it would swap them unasked, so it is refused naming what it holds. A type named twice ("Small" and "small") is refused. **ALL OR NOTHING, READ BACK**: every link and every type's value are read again; the current type is put back as it was. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="array-family-forms"></a>

### Array family forms

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-24 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** repeat one form or one nested family in a row - a linear array - in the family being edited, its count driven by a parameter.

REPEATS ONE FORM IN A ROW in the family open in the Family Editor - a grille's blades, a radiator's fins, a louvre's slots, a rack's shelves - as a linear array: the Family Editor's Array, with its count LABELLED to an Integer family parameter when the types must choose how many. **A LINKED REVIT ARRAY, the kind COPY_ELEMENTS leaves out on purpose** - that tool's loose copies cannot follow a count a type chooses. **ONE FORM PER ARRAY** - a second form takes a second call, and both may follow one count. Every member becomes a model group, the original included, even for one form (measured 2026-10-07, row 5b-358), and `members` names those groups. **OR ONE NESTED FAMILY** (version 2, 2026-10-07) - a coil spring's turns arrayed up. Measured on a scratch family: a level-based nested family moved up, its Bottom locked to a plane, arrayed to its LAST member, and that copy's Top locked to a second plane - the row re-spaced when the planes moved and grew from 3 to 5 with its count. The copies come back IN ORDER ALONG THE ROW, the last one last, for LOCK_NESTED_FAMILY_TO_PLANES. Proved again 2026-10-07 on scratch SpringProof, signed by Ajmal PS. **OR A DETAIL ITEM IN ITS VIEW** (version 4, 2026-11-11) - a view-based nested family, such as a diffuser's flow arrow placed in the Ref. Level plan by PLACE_DETAIL_COMPONENTS, is arrayed in that view, the one it is drawn in, as Array is used on it by hand; where each copy sits is read from its insertion point, since Revit gives it no extent outside its view. Its row stays in the view's plane: a step out of the view is refused by name. **THE COUNT** is a whole number, or an Integer family parameter's name - its value in the current type is the count, and the label lets every type choose. Revit labels an array only with an Integer parameter; a Yes/No is refused by its kind. **THE STEP** is an axis and a distance in millimetres: each member that far on from the one before - or, ending "last", the last member that far from the first and the rest spread evenly between, the one to lock to a plane so the spacing follows a length. **READ BACK, ALL OR NOTHING**: the count, the label and every copy's place are read again. The array's id and the copies' ids come back; copies of a void cut nothing until COMBINE_FAMILY_FORMS combines them. **A DETAIL ITEM WITH NO VIEW** (row 5b-1574, measured 2026-11-12 on Revit 2020): nested in a family, Revit places a detail item on a plane and gives it no Owner View; arrayed in a 3D view it failed with "An internal error has occurred". It is arrayed in the floor plan of the level it stands on, read by its insertion point - four arrows 200 mm apart in Ref. Level, read back. **A FORM ON A PLANE A PARAMETER MOVES** (version 5, row 5b-1261) is arrayed as before, and a finding names the plane and its parameter - and, after the array, any form in the row whose work plane now reads not associated - with FLEX_FAMILY as the next step. `memberForms` gives each copy's own form. **A FORM ALREADY IN AN ARRAY** (version 6, row 5b-1998) is refused before anything is tried - every member of an array is a group, so it is read by its group: the array that holds it is named with its count, its label and its original, and the way on is that array's count, or a form in no array or group. A form in a plain model group is refused naming the group. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="check-family-size-tables"></a>

### Check family size tables

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** does every size_lookup in this family find its table and its column.

Checks the lookup tables of the family open in front against the formulas that read them, and names every size_lookup that cannot find what it asks for - the table, the column, or (version 2) a row for the type's size - type by type. The check to run after a table is imported or renamed, and before the family is loaded into a job. **A LOOKUP THAT MISSES IS SILENT.** size_lookup answers with its DEFAULT when the table it names is not in the family, or the column it asks for is not in that table. The family then builds at the default size, Revit says nothing, and the first sign is a fitting the wrong size in a project weeks later. Reading the table alone (REPORT_FAMILY_TABLES_IN_PROJECT) cannot see this: the table is fine, it is the formula's way to it that is broken. **THE TABLE NAME IS READ PER TYPE.** The first argument of size_lookup is a Text parameter holding the table's name (seen in Revit 2024, docs/43 section 5), and that value can differ between types. One type naming a table that is not there is one type building wrong, so every finding names the type. **WHAT IT FINDS:** a table name that is blank or names no table in the family; a first argument that is not a parameter, or not a Text one; a column that is not in the table; a table or column name that differs only in letter case; a table with no rows; a column other than the first with no name; and, as a note rather than a problem, a table no type names. Each problem is said once however many types share it. **VERSION 2: A ROW FOR EVERY TYPE'S SIZE.** A table and a column that are both there still answer with the default when no row holds the type's size. Each key that is a TYPE parameter holding a number is read in every type, converted into the unit its column's header declares - the unit the table itself is written in - and looked for in the rows, to 0.0001 of that unit. A miss is a NO ROW problem naming the type, the table, the key values and every formula left at its default. Keys are matched from the table's SECOND column on, the first column holding row names: the reading seen in Revit 2024 (docs/43 section 5), with FRAGMENT-ISSUES row 5b-281 still open on its negative half. **WHAT IT STILL DOES NOT CHECK, AND SAYS SO** - each a ROWS NOT CHECKED note, never a pass: a key that is an INSTANCE parameter, whose value is set where the family is placed (a pipe fitting's Nominal Diameter, most often - for those the sizes to check are the pipe segment's, in the project); a key that is an expression rather than one parameter; a key that is text; and a measured key against a column whose header declares no unit, where comparing would mean guessing the unit. **IT NEEDS THE FAMILY OPEN FOR EDITING.** With a project in front it says so rather than reporting no problems, because "nothing wrong" and "you are looking at the wrong document" are different answers. Changes nothing and opens no transaction.

<a id="combine-family-forms"></a>

### Combine family forms

**DRAFT - not yet usable in a chat - refused until proved (D-117).**

**What it does:** join solid forms, or cut a solid form with a void, in the family being edited.

CUTS a solid form with a void, or JOINS solid forms, in the family open in the Family Editor, by combining the forms named into one combination: a void in it cuts the solids, and the solids are made one. The step that turns a void built by a form tool into a hole. Version 2 also lists the family's combinations and takes named ones apart again. **THE ONLY ROUTE THE API HAS IN AN ORDINARY FAMILY.** The solid-cut utility refuses any document that is not a project, a conceptual mass, a curtain panel or an adaptive component, and the project utility's own remarks say it is not available for family documents, 2020 to 2027. A combination is what the Family Editor's own Cut and Join make, and Document.CombineElements makes one. A void made through the API cuts nothing until this - a void drawn by hand cuts what it touches when its sketch is finished, one made by the API does not, which an earlier family build measured five ways. **THE FORMS ARE NAMED BY THEIR IDS** - the ones the form tools gave back, commas between - or SELECTED in the family's window and called `selected`. At least two, and at least one a solid. **THE CUT IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED.** The solids' volume is read before and the combination's after: a void that took nothing away fails the call - it misses the solid, or Revit did not cut with it - and so does a join that came out bigger than its parts. Every solid named must be in the result, read back point by point: one Revit leaves out of the combination refuses the call, found by a trial combination taken back first. **A SOLID ALREADY IN A COMBINATION IS NAMED BY ITS COMBINATION.** Revit's remarks: a solid belongs to at most one, so naming a member would quietly merge two; it is refused with the combination's id. A void may cut several - run this once per body to cut two bodies with one void and keep them apart. **AN ARRAY'S COPY MAY BE NAMED BY ITS GROUP** (version 3, row 5b-358) - the id ARRAY_FAMILY_FORMS gives in `members` stands for the form inside it, and a finding says so. If Revit will not combine a form inside a group, the call is refused in plain words and nothing is kept. Nothing from a call that fails is kept, and Undo, Unjoin Geometry or Uncut Geometry take a combination apart again. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="create-conceptual-form"></a>

### Create conceptual form

**DRAFT - not yet usable in a chat - refused until proved (D-117).**

**What it does:** make a surface, an extrusion, a loft, a sweep or a revolve on lines in an adaptive, pattern-based or mass family, so it follows the points.

Makes a FORM ON LINES in an adaptive component, a pattern-based panel or a mass open in the Family Editor - its Create Form. Built on curves that run through the family's points, the form follows them: the flat glass of a panel that fits every cell of a divided surface, an adaptive fin, a lofted canopy, a two-point beam. These families do not take the classic extrusion, blend, revolve and sweep; this is the form they have - and any other family is refused by name before anything is made. **WHAT IS MADE FOLLOWS FROM WHAT IS GIVEN**, so no kind is asked: ONE closed profile and no depth makes a flat SURFACE filling it; ONE closed profile and a depth makes an EXTRUSION that far along its normal; TWO OR MORE profiles make a LOFT through them in the order given; a PATH makes a SWEEP of one profile along it, or a SWEPT BLEND of several - Revit's rule is a path in one plane, of one curve for a blend, with each profile square to it; an AXIS - one straight line - makes a REVOLVE of one profile about it, a full turn or the angle given, which Revit may return as more than one form. A profile is curve ids, commas between - the ids DRAW_FAMILY_POINT_CURVES gives back - with `|` between profiles; a path is curve ids too. **WHICH SIDE A DEPTH GOES IS A RULE**, not the way the lines were drawn: the profile's normal comes from its curves chained end to end and is turned so the axis it faces most is positive - UP for a profile lying flat, +Y or +X for an upright one; a negative depth goes the other way, and the report names the direction taken. **A PROFILE TO BE FILLED OR PUSHED MUST CLOSE** - a closed circle or ellipse closes by itself - and one to be pushed must be flat and enclose an area; each is refused by name. A void must enclose a volume. **READ BACK, ALL OR NOTHING**: the form, its extent and what it encloses - a solid's volume or a surface's area - are read again; a form holding no geometry fails the call. Its id comes back. **A LOFT REVIT REFUSES IS EXPLAINED**: Revit's own message is followed by what the profiles hold that a loft most often refuses - different numbers of sides, two straight sides on one line, a profile open where the others close, one not flat, two in one plane - or, when none is found, the advice to loft two profiles at a time. Read only after Revit says no, so nothing that lofts is refused first. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="create-family-forms"></a>

### Create family forms

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-23 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** build extrusions, revolves, blends, sweeps and swept blends in the family - one form or a whole list in one call, solid or void, as one undo.

Builds FORMS in the family open in the Family Editor - one extrusion or one revolve, or a list of them, one row per form, solid or void - and gives back every form's id in the order listed. A family of dozens of parts is one call and ONE entry in the undo list. **ONE FORM IS A LIST OF ONE ROW (version 2, 2026-11-01).** CREATE_FAMILY_EXTRUSION and CREATE_FAMILY_REVOLUTION, which built one form a call, were merged into this card and are DEPRECATED: "extrude a circle 300 diameter 500 high" is the row `kind=extrusion workPlane=Ref. Level profile=circle 0,0 150 startMm=0 endMm=500 solid=true`. `formId` gives back the first form's id alone, beside `formIds`, so a step written for those tools' `formId` binds unchanged. The read-back says what theirs said: an extrusion's loops - how many are outlines and how many holes inside them, by where they lie - a revolve's angles and its axis, the plane's facing, and a part-turn's warning to look at which way it swept. **BLENDS, SWEEPS AND SWEPT BLENDS TOO (version 3, 2026-11-01).** CREATE_FAMILY_BLEND, CREATE_FAMILY_SWEEP and CREATE_FAMILY_SWEPT_BLEND were merged into this card and are DEPRECATED. `kind=blend` takes workPlane, baseProfile, topProfile (one loop each), topMm and solid - a square-to-round transition, a hopper; Revit decides which way a blend runs from the way its loops go round, so up to four ways are built and each READ BACK, a wrong one deleted. `kind=sweep` takes workPlane, path - open corners and arcs, the first corner written again for a closed ring - profile, drawn about its own origin, and solid: a handrail, a tube with its bends; the profile's area and the path's length are said beside its volume. `kind=swept blend` takes workPlane, path - ONE straight piece or ONE arc - bottomProfile and topProfile, one loop each, and solid: a reducing elbow. A sweep's id from `formIds` is what SET_FAMILY_SWEEP_PROFILE takes. **EACH ROW STARTS WITH ITS `kind=`** - extrusion, revolve, blend, sweep or swept blend - and carries the single-form tools' own fields: `workPlane`, `profile` and `solid`, then `startMm` and `endMm` for an extrusion, or `axisLine`, `startDegrees` and `endDegrees` for a revolve - written exactly as those tools take them. A row may add `material` (a family material parameter, a material in the family, or "by category"), and `detailLevels` and `views` as SET_FAMILY_FORM_VISIBILITY takes them. **THE LIST IS GIVEN IN THE VALUE, OR AS A FILE** - the full path of a text file in the temporary folder, one row per line, lines starting # ignored. A long list is written to the file once, under %TEMP%\heron-work, rather than typed into every call. That folder is read even where Revit keeps its own temporary folder in a sub-folder of the user's (5b-430). **ALL OR NOTHING.** Every row is checked before anything is built, each problem named with its row. Each form is then read back as the single-form tools read theirs - its extent, a solid's volume, a material and where it shows - and one row Revit refuses or that reads back wrong keeps nothing of the whole list. **A VOID CUTS NOTHING BY BEING MADE** - COMBINE_FAMILY_FORMS cuts it into a solid, by the ids given back. **LOOPS THAT TOUCH ARE REFUSED, AND SO IS AN OVERSIZED CALL (version 4, 2026-11-20).** Loops of one profile that share a corner or a side, or cross, are named by row and loop before anything is made: a ring is an outer loop with an inner one inside it, crossing strips are forms of their own. More than 600 loops in one call is refused with the count - about 300 a call builds well inside the time one call is given. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="create-family-freeform-solid"></a>

### Create family freeform solid

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-26 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** loft through sections or sweep along a 3D path as one smooth, fixed freeform form in a family, solid or void.

Makes ONE SMOOTH FORM in the family open in the Family Editor where the classic forms cannot: a LOFT through two or more sections placed anywhere and facing any way - an animal's body, a hull, a horn - or a SWEEP of a profile along a path that leaves the plane - a spring's wire, a hose, a rail bent in three directions. One form where many stacked pieces would be slow and heavy, as a SOLID or a VOID. **NOT PARAMETRIC.** It is a FREEFORM form: a fixed shape, kept as it was made. It has no sketch, no parameter drives it, it moves with no reference plane, and a flex cannot change it. To change its size, delete it and make it again. Where an extrusion, a revolve, a blend or a sweep in one plane can make the shape, those are the better tool, because parameters can drive them. **EVERYTHING IS MILLIMETRES IN THE FAMILY'S OWN X,Y,Z FROM ITS ORIGIN**, except a loop, written in its own two coordinates: the first runs level across it, the second up it, and a level loop takes X and Y - so a section facing X is written in Y,Z and one facing Y in X,Z, as the other form tools write their planes. A loop is `circle CX,CY R`, `ellipse CX,CY RX RY`, `rect X1,Y1 X2,Y2`, `polygon CX,CY R N`, a smooth `spline X,Y; X,Y; X,Y; X,Y`, or corners and arcs `X,Y; X,Y; arc MX,MY X,Y`. A circle or an ellipse may end with how many pieces it is cut into, 2 when left out. **A LOFT** takes sections with `|` between, each `at X,Y,Z facing X: <loop>` - facing X, Y, Z or a direction NX,NY,NZ - and runs through them in the order written. Every section must be cut into the SAME NUMBER OF PIECES: Revit pairs them piece by piece and builds unequal counts distorted (measured), so they are refused. A circle or an ellipse is started level with the section before it, so a rectangle lofted into a circle does not twist. **A SWEEP** takes a profile - one loop, or several with `|` between for a hollow one - laid square to the path's start, and a path: `helix CX,CY,CZ R PITCH TURNS` (round Z, or X or Y, and `left` for a left hand), `spline X,Y,Z; X,Y,Z; X,Y,Z` through points, or pieces `X,Y,Z; X,Y,Z; arc MX,MY,MZ X,Y,Z`. A path that would run into itself - crossing itself, turns closer than the wire is thick, a bend tighter than the profile - is REFUSED BY NAME before Revit sees it: Revit builds one without complaint, as a solid that is not whole (measured). **A VOID CUTS NOTHING BY BEING MADE** - COMBINE_FAMILY_FORMS cuts a solid with it. Its material is LINK_FAMILY_PARAMETER. **READ BACK, ALL OR NOTHING.** The form must have an extent and a solid a volume, both reported. Any refusal from Revit fails the call and nothing is kept. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="create-reference-planes"></a>

### Create reference planes

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-12 (Revit 2020, 2024).

**What it does:** add named reference planes to the family being edited, at these distances.

Adds NAMED reference planes to the family open in the Family Editor, each at a distance in millimetres from the family's origin, all facing one way: planes that control left-right position, front-back position, or height. "Box Left at -300, Box Right at 300" is one call; the height planes another. The skeleton every parametric family is built on - geometry is locked to these planes and dimensions labelled between them. **THE AXES ARE THE FAMILY'S OWN.** Left is minus X and right plus X, front is minus Y and back plus Y, as the template's own elevations are set out. A left-right plane is drawn in the floor plan, a height plane in an elevation, because a horizontal plane cannot be drawn in plan. **EVERY PLANE IS READ BACK BEFORE IT IS KEPT.** Its normal must lie along the axis asked for and its position must be the distance asked for. A plane that came out tilted is reported from an earlier family build - a point passed where Revit wanted a direction - and nothing checks it later, so a plane that does not read back true fails the whole call and nothing is kept. **A NAME ALREADY IN THE FAMILY** - a level's included, because every later step finds planes and levels by name - is refused unless it is a plane that already sits where it was asked for, which is left alone, so a request run twice adds nothing twice. A plane of that name somewhere ELSE refuses the whole call: moving it would drag whatever is locked to it, and that is a decision for the modeller, not a side effect. **IT DOES NOT TRIM OR STRETCH THE LINES.** Each plane is drawn across the origin, comfortably past the distances in the call. How far a plane's line runs is a model property that shows in every view at once, and judging it is done by eye in Revit - reported from an earlier family build, where changes to plane extents were undone by hand both times. Is Reference is left at Revit's default; SET_FAMILY_PLANE_REFERENCE sets it, and Defines Origin. **ALL OR NOTHING.** Every name is checked before the first plane is made, and a refusal from Revit afterwards fails the call with nothing kept. **OR AT AN ANGLE (version 2, 2026-11-12)** - axis "angle", each plane Name=degrees: a VERTICAL plane drawn in the floor plan through a point (throughMm, "X,Y" in mm - the origin when left out), its line turned that many degrees from the left-right line towards the back: 30 runs up to the right, -15 down to the right. What an angle label between two planes needs. Read back the same way - horizontal normal at the angle asked, through the point - and a plane of that name already there at that angle through that point is left alone. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="delete-family-parameters"></a>

### Delete family parameters

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-06 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** delete these family parameters from the family being edited, when nothing uses them - a dimension label taken off first only when asked.

Deletes FAMILY parameters, by name, from the family open in the Family Editor - the Family Types dialog's "Delete Parameter", several at a time. For the leftovers of a family build: a parameter added and never used, or one whose job moved to another. **IT DELETES ONLY WHAT NOTHING ELSE USES, AND IT NEVER CASCADES.** Before anything goes, each name is checked for everything that would change when it went, and refused BY NAME with what still uses it: another parameter's FORMULA that reads it (each formula quoted); a DIMENSION labelled with it (how many); an ARRAY whose count it is; a FORM FIELD linked to it - Extrusion Start or End, Visible, Material; a NESTED FAMILY's parameter linked to it; a CONNECTOR whose size follows it. The refusal says what to unhook first. Nothing else is unhooked here - taking a parameter out from under a form or a formula changes the family somewhere the modeller is not looking. **ONE EXCEPTION, ONLY WHEN ASKED: A DIMENSION'S LABEL.** With `unlabelFirst` true, a dimension labelled with a parameter being deleted does not block it - the label is taken off first (Label: <None>), then the parameter is deleted, in the same call and the same Undo. For "delete this parameter even though it labels a dimension", or "unlabel the dimension and delete the parameter". The dimension stays, unlabelled, and the planes do not move: an unlabelled dimension drives nothing. Every dimension unlabelled is listed - the two planes it measures, its view, its reading - and read back after Revit regenerates: no label left, the same reading. Formulas, arrays, form fields, nested links and connectors still block exactly as they do without it, and any one of them refuses the whole call before a single label comes off. Without `unlabelFirst`, a label blocks as it always has (version 2; version 1 had no way past it). A parameter whose OWN formula is set, and which nothing else uses, CAN go - its formula reads others, nobody reads it. A formula user that is itself in the list does not block: asking for both deletes both, the user first. **A NAME NOT FOUND IS NEVER GUESSED.** Names are matched exactly; a name the family does not have is refused with the nearest names it does have. Revit's built-in parameters for the category are refused too. **ALL OR NOTHING.** Every name is checked before the first goes, and one refusal refuses the call. Each deletion is read back - the family no longer has that name - and a deletion Revit refuses, or one that did not take, fails the call with nothing kept. One Undo puts every deleted parameter back with its values. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

| **You get** | deleted, unlabelled, findings |

<a id="divide-family-surface"></a>

### Divide family surface

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-26 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** divide a face of a form in a mass or conceptual family into a U and V grid, and give it a tile pattern or a panel family.

DIVIDES A SURFACE in a mass, an adaptive component or a pattern-based panel open in the Family Editor - the conceptual Family Editor's Divide Surface: a U and a V grid laid on one face of a form, so a pattern-based panel family can fill every cell - a facade's panels, a canopy's glazing. **THE FORM BY ITS ID, THE FACE BY WHICH WAY IT FACES.** The form is the id CREATE_CONCEPTUAL_FORM gave back; the face is top, bottom, front, back, left or right, or "largest" when not said - chosen only from the faces Revit's own CanBeDivided accepts. A face already divided is refused with its surface's id. **EACH GRID A NUMBER OR A DISTANCE.** "10" is Revit's Number for that direction, "1500 mm" a fixed distance; empty leaves Revit's default layout. Both centred, unrotated, with no offset. Whether Number counts the cells or the lines between them is not promised: the gridline count Revit made is reported, and BV21 records it. **THE PATTERN OR PANEL, OPTIONAL**: a tile pattern by name - Rectangle, Hexagon - or a loaded pattern-based panel family's type, "Panel : Glass", chosen only from the types Revit lists as valid for this surface. A name Revit does not offer is refused, naming what it does offer, and nothing is kept (version 3). **READ BACK, ALL OR NOTHING**: the surface's host, each grid's layout and value, its gridline counts and its type are read again; one that does not read as asked fails the call. The surface's id comes back. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="draw-family-detail-lines"></a>

### Draw family detail lines

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** draw lines from a typed shape - a 2D family's lines in its view, locked to the planes they lie on, or a project's detail lines in a view or model lines on a plane.

Draws the LINES of a 2D family - a profile, a detail item, an annotation symbol, a title block - in its view, as the Family Editor's Line tool does there: detail lines. In a PROFILE family every line is part of the profile, so the loops given ARE the profile - closed loops that do not cross, a loop inside another a hole - and an open path is refused there, as are loops that cross or touch, checked edge by edge before anything is drawn. **THE SAME SHAPE LANGUAGE AS THE FORM TOOLS**, millimetres in the view's own two model coordinates: closed "circle", "rect", "polygon" or corners, and open "path X,Y; X,Y" pieces, `|` between. **LOCKED TO THE PLANES THEY LIE ON, WHEN ASKED** - every straight line lying along a NAMED reference plane is aligned and locked to it, so the profile resizes when a labelled dimension moves the plane. That is the step that makes a profile parametric. A line is locked only where it already lies; one on no named plane is left free and counted. ONE PLANE PER LINE: where named planes coincide, the one that does not define the origin is the one locked to, and two such planes are refused as ambiguous rather than both locked. **ON A SUBCATEGORY** of the family's category for its line weight, made when new, or "none" for the category itself. **AND IN A PROJECT (version 2, 2026-11-01)** - CREATE_LINE was merged into this card and is DEPRECATED. `lineKind` says DETAIL lines, drawn in the view named and printed with it alone, or MODEL lines, real lines in the model on the plane `planeMm` along the view's direction - with no view, a horizontal plane at that height. There is no safe default, so in a project it is asked for; a 3D view holds no detail lines. The style is one of the project's line styles or "none". All or nothing in millimetres: a piece shorter than Revit's shortest line refuses the call. **A 3D MODEL FAMILY IS REFUSED** - its 2D symbol is DRAW_FAMILY_SYMBOLIC_LINES. READ BACK, ALL OR NOTHING: every line's ends, its style and every lock are read again. Their ids come back. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

### Draw family filled region

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** draw a filled or masking region - a hatch or mask in a project view, or inside the family being edited: a detail item's hatch, a symbol's mask, a solid plan fill.

Draws a FILLED or MASKING region in a project's view, or inside the family open in the Family Editor - the hatch of a detail item's insulation, the solid of a cut steel section, the white mask a symbol hides what is under it with, the solid fill of a plan symbol in a model family. The Family Editor's Filled Region and Masking Region. **THE KIND OF FAMILY AND THE RELEASE DECIDE WHAT EXISTS.** A 2D family - a detail item, an annotation, a profile, a title block - draws in its VIEW, by the view's name, on every release 2020 to 2027. A 3D model family draws on a level or a named reference plane, and Revit has a call for that only from 2023. A MASKING region has a call of its own only from 2024. Each is found on the running Revit by its own signature; a release without it is refused by name with what to do instead. **THE SAME SHAPE LANGUAGE AS THE FORM TOOLS**, millimetres in the plane's own two model coordinates, closed loops only, `|` between them - a loop inside another is a hole. **THE TYPE IS NAMED** - the family's own filled region type, "Solid Black", or "masking". A name the family does not hold is refused with the ones it does. **READ BACK, ALL OR NOTHING**: the region, its loops, its type and whether it is masking are read again; one that does not read as asked fails the call. Its id comes back. **In a project, it exists in ONE view and nowhere else** (version 2, from CREATE_FILLED_REGION) - the drafting patch: a shaft marked up, an area shaded on a key plan, a zone coloured on a coordination drawing. A filled region is annotation, not model: it is on no other drawing, not in the model, and in no schedule, and the answer says so. The view must take annotation - a plan, a section, an elevation, a detail, a drafting view, a legend or a sheet; a 3D view is refused with the reason. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

The curves' ids come back for CREATE_CONCEPTUAL_FORM. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="extrude-between-planes"></a>

### Extrude between planes

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-24 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** build a solid box between these family planes, locked to them.

Builds a rectangular SOLID extrusion in the family open in the Family Editor, exactly between four named side planes, standing on a base (a level or a horizontal plane) and reaching up to a top plane - and LOCKS its four side faces and its top face to those planes. The body of an air terminal, the neck on top of it, a casing: any box a parametric family is made of. **LOCKED IS THE WHOLE POINT.** A box drawn at the same coordinates as the planes is not tied to them: move the planes and it stays where it was, while looking parametric right up until someone flexes it - reported from an earlier family build. So every face is aligned and locked to its plane, the base is sketched ON the base plane so it follows it, and if any one of the five locks cannot be made the whole call fails and no box is left behind. **THE PROFILE IS SKETCHED FLAT, ON THE BASE.** Face references come back reliably from a sketch on a horizontal plane - reported from an earlier family build, where a sketch stood on a vertical plane gave a reference for one face of six. A box sitting on top of another - a neck on a body - is built with the top of the lower one as its base. **THE FAMILY'S AXES ARE TAKEN FROM THE PLANES.** Two of the four side planes must control left-right and two front-back; which name is which does not matter. The size is read back from the box after it is locked and must match the planes, or nothing is kept. **SOLID ONLY, AND BOXES ONLY.** A void is not built here: a void made through the API cuts nothing on its own - an earlier family build measured five ways and found no volume change - and the cut is COMBINE_FAMILY_FORMS's, which measures it. Any other shape, round ones included, is CREATE_FAMILY_FORMS's, and a round size is labelled by LABEL_FAMILY_RADIUS. This card said until 2026-10-01 that a circle's size cannot be driven through the API on Revit 2020; that was measured for a PROJECT, and in a family the calls exist on every release - whether the label drives the circle is NEEDS-CHECKING BM3 (row 5b-261). **ITS ID COMES BACK (version 2)** as `formId`, the box's unique id - what a later step names it by: LINK_FAMILY_PARAMETER's `forms` for a material or Visible, SET_FAMILY_FORM_VISIBILITY, ARRAY_FAMILY_FORMS. The box is also handed on as `elements`. No REPORT_FAMILY_FORMS call is needed to find it. **IT BUILDS GEOMETRY AND NOTHING ELSE.** Material, visibility and subcategory are set in Properties; the planes' positions are decided by CREATE_REFERENCE_PLANES and LABEL_FAMILY_DIMENSION before this runs. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="extrude-polygon-between-planes"></a>

### Extrude polygon between planes

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-24 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** build a regular polygon prism - a hexagon - whose across-flats size follows a parameter.

Builds a REGULAR POLYGON PRISM in the family open in the Family Editor - a hexagon above all: a bolt head, a nut, a hex bar - whose size across the flats FOLLOWS A LENGTH PARAMETER, standing on a base (a level or a horizontal plane) and reaching up to a top plane. An even number of sides, 4 to 12, centred on the family's origin, one pair of flats facing front and back. **WHY A TOOL OF ITS OWN.** A polygon drawn with CREATE_FAMILY_FORMS is fixed: nothing ties its slanted sides to anything, and EXTRUDE_BETWEEN_PLANES builds boxes only, between planes that run left-right and front-back. So this one makes a vertical reference plane for EVERY side, named after the parameter ("Across Flats Side 1" ...), and for each pair of opposite sides a dimension labelled with the parameter and an EQ about a plane through the origin - the family's own Center (Front/Back) or Center (Left/Right) where the pair faces that way, otherwise a plane made through the origin and pinned there. Every side face of the prism is then aligned and locked to its plane, and the top face to the top plane. Measured 2026-10-24 on Revit 2020: a hexagon labelled this way read 46 and 10 mm across the flats, and 53.1 and 11.5 mm across the corners, when the parameter was set to 46 and 10. **THE PARAMETER MUST ALREADY HOLD THE SIZE** - a new length reads 0, and a label on 0 collapses the planes - so it is checked before anything is made. Planes of those names already in the family refuse the call: it is built once. Any lock or label that cannot be made throws, and the whole call is rolled back - no prism left half tied. **IT BUILDS GEOMETRY AND NOTHING ELSE.** Material, visibility and the hole of a nut are other tools' - a round void and LABEL_FAMILY_RADIUS for the hole, COMBINE_FAMILY_FORMS for the cut. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="flex-family"></a>

### Flex family

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-23 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** flex the family through these sizes, read the geometry back, and put everything back.

FLEXES the family open in the Family Editor: tries it at each set of sizes given - "Width=900; Depth=500 | Width=400; Depth=700" - reads the geometry back at every one, then puts every value back as it was and proves it did. The test a modeller runs by typing new sizes into Family Types and watching the family follow, with the watching done by measurement. **IT MEASURES THE GEOMETRY, NOT THE PLANES.** Planes that move prove the dimensions work, not that anything followed them - reported from an earlier family build, where a box drawn without locks looked parametric right up to its first flex. So each trial reads EVERY solid's own extent - a neck moving inside a body that does not is invisible in the whole - and every labelled dimension and every connector tied to a parameter is compared with what that parameter holds. When the labelled planes moved and no solid did, that is said in those words. **AND EVERY NESTED FAMILY** (version 3, row 5b-367) - each one's own extent is read beside the solids, judged the same way, and must come back where it started; a spring's arrayed turns are measured, not only its end forms. **EACH TRIAL STARTS FROM THE FAMILY AS IT WAS**, plus only the values that trial names. Use sizes that are really different and not square - a square trial alone hides a width and a depth swapped. **IT CHANGES THE FAMILY AND CHANGES IT BACK, AND SAYS SO.** It writes values, so it is a MODIFY: it is not a read and does not pretend to be one. Every value it touched is written back afterwards and read back, and the solid is measured again against how it started. If the family does not come back exactly as it was, the call fails and nothing from it is kept. **A TRIAL REVIT CANNOT SOLVE FAILS THE CALL**, naming the trial and the dimension that could not reach its value, and nothing is kept - constraints that cannot be satisfied at some size are exactly what a flex exists to find, and Revit itself may only warn about them. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

2. Turn **Changes** on in Heron's **Settings** (Heron tab).
3. In a Claude chat, ask in your own words, for example *"flex the family"*. Say the values under **You say** in the same sentence.
4. Heron makes the change as **one entry in Revit's Undo list**. With **Ask to Keep** on, Revit asks **Keep or Discard** first; Ctrl+Z takes it back.

Other ways to ask: *"flex this family at 900 by 500 and 400 by 700"* · *"try the family at different sizes and put it back"*

<a id="label-family-dimension"></a>

### Label family dimension

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-12 (Revit 2020, 2024).

**What it does:** tie the distance between two family planes to a parameter, kept centred if asked - or the angle between two planes that meet to an angle parameter.

Dimensions two parallel reference planes of the family open in the Family Editor and LABELS that dimension with a family parameter, so the parameter drives how far apart they are - "Box Left to Box Right is Width". With a centre plane named as well, it also adds the EQ dimension across the three, so the two planes move equally either side of the centre instead of one edge doing all the moving. This is the step that makes a family parametric. **THE PARAMETER MUST ALREADY HOLD THE DISTANCE THE PLANES ARE APART.** The moment a dimension is labelled, Revit moves the planes to the parameter's value. A new length reads zero, so labelling first collapses the planes onto each other and the skeleton is gone - reported from an earlier family build. So the distance is measured and compared with the parameter first, and a difference of more than half a millimetre refuses the call with both numbers, naming SET_FAMILY_TYPE_VALUES. **ONE LABEL PER PARAMETER, AND PER PAIR OF PLANES.** A parameter that already labels a dimension is refused a second one, and so is a pair of planes that a labelled dimension already measures: two dimensions driving one parameter fight as soon as anything moves - reported from an earlier family build, where a rebuild left the old plane-to-plane dimension behind beside its replacement. **THE EQ NEEDS THE CENTRE PLANE MIDWAY.** An EQ dimension moves the planes until both sides are equal, so a centre plane that is not already midway is refused rather than quietly shifting the geometry. Both plan axes are usually centred - the family's insertion point then sits in the middle of the box - and the base-to-top height usually is not. **A LEVEL COUNTS AS A PLANE**, so a height is labelled from Ref. Level to a top plane. Left-right and front-back dimensions are drawn in the floor plan, heights in an elevation, placed outside the planes so they stay readable. **ALL OR NOTHING, READ BACK AFTER REVIT REGENERATES.** The label, the EQ, the distance the dimension reads and where every plane now sits are read after the regeneration; a plane that moved or a reading that differs fails the call, and nothing is kept. **WHICH END A FLEX WOULD MOVE IS SAID FIRST** (version 2). When the parameter changes, Revit moves whichever end of the labelled dimension is least held. Each end is read before the label is made, in three grades: a level, a pinned plane or one that defines the origin is held FAST - a flex never moves it, except a level nobody pinned, which a flex moves when the other end is pinned (5b-1332); a plane that a labelled dimension drives from elsewhere, or that an EQ or a lock ties to another plane or level, is held SOFTLY - a flex moves it only through that chain; a plane none of those touch is FREE, Revit's first choice to move. Seen on Revit 2020: a height labelled from a new, free plane to a plane carrying two other labels moved the FREE plane when flexed, and did until that plane was pinned. So a free end beside a softly held one, or two free ends, is named in `freeEnd` and the findings as the end a flex may move - *pin it (SET_PIN_STATE) or dimension it to a level*. A free end beside one held fast is the ordinary height from Ref. Level: the free end is the only one a flex can move, so the findings say so and nothing is warned of. Two ends held fast have nothing a flex can move, and the findings say that - unless one is a level nobody pinned: then the findings say the flex moves the level, and every form on it, and to unpin the other end. With a centre plane the EQ moves both ends equally, so no end is free on its own. The label is still made in every case: a free end is a warning, not a refusal. Nothing is pinned unasked (Article 7); `pinFreeEnd=true` pins the free end - the first named, when both are - before the label and reads the pin back, and pins nothing, saying why, where a pin would leave the flex nothing to move or fight the EQ. Two planes in the same place are refused as before, and that refusal names the same route. A lock or an EQ to geometry ties the geometry to the plane, not the plane to anything, and does not count; a lock or EQ running between the two ends is named as what the label will fight; a plain dimension holds nothing. **AN ANGLE TOO (version 3, 2026-11-11, FRAGMENT-ISSUES 5b-1498).** When the parameter named is an ANGLE, the two planes are two reference planes that MEET - "Arrow Left" and "Arrow Right", both upright, seen in Ref. Level - and the label is an angular dimension on an arc centred where they cross, drawn in the floor plan (two upright planes) or the elevation that looks along the line they meet on. The same safety order as a distance: the parameter must already hold the angle the planes make - on one side of where they cross or the other, 30 or 150 degrees say - checked before anything is made, a difference refusing the call with both numbers; one label per parameter and per pair of planes; read back after the regeneration - the label, the angle it reads, and neither plane turned or moved. Parallel planes make no angle and are refused; a centre plane (an EQ) is for a distance and is refused with an angle; a level is not taken - draw a reference plane on it. Which plane a flex turns is said from what holds each FAST (pinned, or defining the origin), and `pinFreeEnd` pins the first named when neither is - but which one Revit turns, and about what point, is not yet measured (Group NE). A LENGTH parameter takes version 2's path exactly as before. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Changes the model (`MODIFY`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **You say** | **from plane** - text<br>**to plane** - text<br>**parameter name** - text<br>**centre plane** - text<br>**pin free end** - yes or no - true or false; optional |
| **You get** | labelled, free end, pinned end, equalised, angle degrees, distance mm, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2020, 2024 |
| **Capability** | `LABEL_FAMILY_DIMENSION` |

4. Heron makes the change as **one entry in Revit's Undo list**. With **Ask to Keep** on, Revit asks **Keep or Discard** first; Ctrl+Z takes it back.

<a id="label-family-radius"></a>

### Label family radius

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-12 (Revit 2020, 2024).

**What it does:** tie the radius or diameter of a round family form, inside its sketch, or of a 2D arc drawn as a detail or symbolic line, to a length parameter.

LABELS the round size of a form in the family open in the Family Editor with a length parameter, so the parameter drives it: a duct neck's diameter, a pipe stub's size, a bell's radius. The dimension goes INSIDE THE FORM'S SKETCH, where Edit Extrusion or Edit Revolve shows it - the way a modeller does it by hand. LABEL_FAMILY_DIMENSION is the straight distance between two planes; this is the round size. **ON THE SKETCH, NEVER ON THE FINISHED EDGE.** Version 1 labelled the finished form's round edge. Revit accepted the label and the circle ignored it: on 2026-10-03 the stem of a gate valve in Family1 (Revit 2024) read 8 mm with its parameter at 14, and FLEX_FAMILY refused (row 5b-305, NEEDS-CHECKING BM3). A dimension on the sketch's own curve drove the form at 300 and at 40 mm the same evening - on a form made in that run and on one made days before - so a form already built can be labelled now. **TWO KINDS OF ROUND SIZE.** An EXTRUSION's circle: a radial or diameter dimension on a sketched arc of that radius. A REVOLVE's radius: a straight dimension, in the sketch, from a REFERENCE PLANE the axis lies on to the profile line running alongside the axis, with the axis locked to that plane. Measured from the revolve's own axis line, Revit moved the axis and the revolve broke, so a revolve with no plane through its axis is refused - make one with CREATE_REFERENCE_PLANES first. A distance from the axis is a radius: give it a radius parameter whose formula halves the diameter. Other forms are refused. **A TORUS - A REVOLVE WHOSE PROFILE IS A CIRCLE - HAS TWO MORE** (version 3, row 5b-306). The TUBE: the circle's own radius or diameter, labelled on its sketched arc as an extrusion's is. The RING: the circle centre's distance from the axis, labelled the way a modeller does it by hand - from the plane the axis lies on to a reference plane through the circle's centre, with the centre locked to that plane. The plane is made, named after the parameter, when the family has none. A plane already labelled with the same parameter is used as it is, not refused as a second label. A dimension straight to the centre point is refused by Revit, so it is never tried. Measured 2026-10-03 on scratch families: a tube from 40 to 80 and 10, a ring from 200 to 400 and 60. When one value is more than one size of the revolve, the call is refused and the label is left for Edit Revolve. THE RING IS HELD BACK since 2026-10-24 (row 5b-1333): on Revit 2020 a ring labelled this way moved three OTHER forms with its plane at the first flex, so the ring is refused and left for Edit Revolve; the tube is still labelled. **A SWEPT BLEND HAS THREE** (version 4, 2026-10-07, for a coil spring's half-turns). Its PATH's arc radius, with the arc's centre locked to the planes through it; every PROFILE circle's own radius or diameter, a half circle's arc included; and a profile circle CENTRE's height off the path's plane - a coil's rise - from the level or plane the path is on to a plane through the centre, made and named after the parameter, the centre locked to it. One parameter may label the same kind of size on several swept blends; a rise reuses its plane. Measured on scratch families: radius 40 to 60 and 25, wire 5 to 8 and 3, rise 15 to 30 and 6, each followed. Proved again 2026-10-07 on scratch SpringProof, signed by Ajmal PS. **BOTH REFERENCES ARE CHECKED BEFORE REVIT IS ASKED** (version 5, 2026-10-22, row 5b-1318). On Revit 2020 the revolve route threw Revit's own "Invalid number of references" three times in the owner's floor drain families - a trap's two outlet sockets and a floor-based host's end disc, in an elevation and in a plan, from a made plane and from a template one - while the extrusion route labelled three sketched circles in the same session. Revit says that when one of the two references it is handed is not one it will measure to. Version 5 reads the plane's reference and the profile line's (or the centre plane's) before the call - that each exists and names the element it should - and refuses in one sentence naming which one is missing and the release when one is not; each reference's kind is read and said (a surface for a plane, a line for a sketch curve are what a straight dimension is expected to take), but a kind other than that is a note, not a refusal - which kinds Revit takes is Revit's to say. When Revit refuses the dimension with both in hand, it is asked again with each reference read back from its written form, so the answer names the one Revit would not take as first read; and the sentence that reaches the modeller is Heron's, counting the tries made, with Revit's words after it in quotes, never Revit's alone. A labelled call's answer says what was read of both. Which reference it is on 2020 is NOT known: NEEDS-CHECKING Group IS asks Revit, on 2020 and again on 2024. The extrusion and swept blend routes are untouched. **A 2D ARC TOO** (version 6, 2026-11-11) - a DETAIL or SYMBOLIC line that is an arc, named by its id: a plan symbol's round end, a detail item's curved arrow. A radial dimension - a diameter one for a diameter parameter - goes on the arc itself in the arc's own view: a detail line's Owner View; a symbolic line's Owner View where Revit gives one, else the plan or elevation looking straight at the plane it is drawn on. The same rules as a form's: the parameter must already hold the arc's size, one label per parameter, and the label, the value and the arc's own radius are read back. A straight line is refused - it has no radius; its planes are labelled by LABEL_FAMILY_DIMENSION. **ONE FAMILY RESIZES WITH THE PIPE SIZE.** With the round sizes labelled, one body follows Nominal Diameter through formulas, instead of one shape set per size switched on and off. **THE PARAMETER MUST ALREADY HOLD THE SIZE.** A label moves the geometry to the parameter's value - a new length reads zero - so the curve labelled is the one whose size the parameter already holds (half of it, for a diameter), and a form with none is refused, listing the sizes it has. **ONE LABEL PER PARAMETER**, as LABEL_FAMILY_DIMENSION: a second dimension driving the same parameter fights the first. **THE FORM IS NAMED BY ITS ID** - the one its form tool gave back - or SELECTED in the family's window and called `selected`. **ALL OR NOTHING, READ BACK** after Revit regenerates: the dimension must carry the parameter and read its value. FLEX_FAMILY at two different sizes shows the form following. **A FAMILY'S DIMENSION BELONGS TO NO VIEW** (row 5b-1572, measured 2026-11-12 on Revit 2020): the label on a 2D arc reads back with no Owner View, and that is right; one in ANOTHER view is refused. Kept and flexed: a detail arc labelled "Arc Radius" followed it from 150 to 200 mm. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="link-family-parameter"></a>

### Link family parameter

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-24 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** associate a family parameter: link or unlink a parameter of elements in the family - by category, particular forms, nested copies, lines, regions or model text by id, or a nested type - or set a form's material, and read it back.

Links a parameter of elements ALREADY in the family open in the Family Editor to one of the family's own parameters, or unlinks it, and reads every link back - the "Associate Family Parameter" button at the end of a row in Properties, for every element the call names at once. A duct connector's Flow or size, a solid's Material or Visible: whatever Revit lets be linked. **ONE TOOL FOR "ASSOCIATE FAMILY PARAMETER" (version 3, 2026-11-01).** LINK_FAMILY_FORM_PARAMETER, SET_FAMILY_FORM_MATERIAL and LINK_NESTED_TYPE_PARAMETER were merged into this card and are DEPRECATED. The elements are named ONE way a call: by category, as before; or PARTICULAR forms and nested copies by the ids the form tools or PLACE_FAMILY_INSTANCES gave back, or `selected` (`forms`) - one form's Visible, a revolve's End Angle, one copy's Thread Size, its other copies left alone; or a nested family's TYPE by its family and type (`family`, `type`) - the motor's Width following Motor Width. A form's Material is LINKED to a family material parameter, or SET to a material the family holds ("Material=Steel"), or put back with "Material=by category"; a field already linked is unlinked before a material is written into it, and the answer says so. A void has no material and is refused. A reporting parameter cannot drive anything and is refused. A TYPE parameter asked of a nested copy is refused naming family= and type=; an instance parameter asked of a nested type is refused naming the copy. The Material-of-a-form word conflict between those cards ends here: there is one tool. **THE ELEMENTS ARE NAMED, NEVER GUESSED.** A category as Revit or the Properties palette names it - "Duct Connector", "Pipe Connector", "Extrusion", a nested family's name - or "all", and for connectors a system classification such as "Return Air", or "all". A name that takes nothing is refused with what the family has. **THE LINKS ARE PAIRS**, element parameter = family parameter, semicolons between; "none" in place of a family parameter unlinks. **A LINK REVIT WOULD REFUSE IS REFUSED FIRST.** A family parameter that does not exist, or holds a different kind of value - a Length cannot drive an Air Flow - is refused naming both parameters and both kinds, with the ones that could drive it, before anything changes. So is a parameter Revit does not let be linked at all. **EVERY LINK IS READ BACK**, before and after, per element, on one line. One already as asked is reported "already linked" and not counted as a change. **ALL OR NOTHING, ONE UNDO.** Everything is checked before the first link; a refusal from Revit part-way fails the call, and Heron rolls the whole call back. The links live in the family: a project's placed units follow them only once the family is loaded into it again. **VERSION 2 (2026-09-29, FRAGMENT-ISSUES 5b-260).** Three edge cases a review found after version 1 was signed are fixed, and a fourth waits on a measurement in Revit - NEEDS-CHECKING BD5. This is version 2; version 1's proof no longer describes the code and is kept as a record, and the fragment is DRAFT until it is proved again. **VERSION 4 (2026-11-11, FRAGMENT-ISSUES 5b-1497): A FAMILY'S 2D TOO.** The ids in `forms`, or what is `selected`, may also name a detail line (straight, arc, ellipse or spline), a symbolic line, a filled or masking region, or model text - a plan arrow's Visible linked to "Show Arrow", a symbolic outline's Visible to a Yes/No - for whatever parameter Revit lets be linked on it. Anything that is none of these, nor a form or a nested copy, is still refused by name. The answer names them as the Properties palette does ("Symbolic Line id N", "Masking Region id N"). This is version 4: version 3's proof is kept as the record, and the tool is DRAFT until NEEDS-CHECKING Group NE proves it again. **VERSION 6 (2026-11-22): A REFERENCE POINT TOO** - its Offset off the plane it is hosted on, a folded pattern panel's tip, linked to a Length family parameter such as "Tip Depth"; named "Reference Point id N". **VERSION 7 (2026-11-24, FRAGMENT-ISSUES 5b-2013): A PLAIN ID TOO.** The ids in `forms` may be the element id Revit and every read tool print - a number such as 9659268 - as well as a unique id; version 6 took the unique id only and refused the number as naming nothing. An id that names nothing is still refused, and the refusal says both kinds are taken. DRAFT until NEEDS-CHECKING Group QE proves it again. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="load-family"></a>

### Load family

**DRAFT - not yet usable in a chat - refused until proved (D-117).**

**What it does:** load this family file into the project or a family, or reload it over the loaded one.

Loads one `.rfa` family file into the open project - or into a family document, which is how a nested family gets in - and reports what arrived: its types, and every material the load added or changed. **Reloading a family that is already there is asked for, never assumed.** With `reload` left off, a family of the same name is REFUSED by name, as version 1 did. `reload=true` is Revit's "Overwrite the existing version" - the file's family, with the types' parameter values already in the target kept; `reload=true` with `overwriteValues=true` is "Overwrite the existing version and its parameter values". A shared nested family inside the file takes the file's version too. Use it after a family - a nested component like a nut in a support - has been edited and SAVED: a reload reads the file on disk, not the window it is open in. **A reload can overwrite same-named materials in the target with no dialog naming it**, so materials are read before and after and every one that moved is listed, colour and all. Each material is compared with ITSELF, by its element id - a project can hold several materials of one name, and a name held more than once is labelled with the id and said in `findings`. Constitution Article 7 puts family reloads among the operations that need explicit confirmation, so `reload=true` is never defaulted and a caller should confirm it with the modeller first. **A file open in Revit with unsaved changes is refused** - a load reads the file, not the window, so it would bring in whatever the file last held.
