<a id="lock-family-lines-to-planes"></a>

### Lock family lines to planes

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-12 (Revit 2020, 2024).

**What it does:** lock a 2D family's lines and filled region edges to named planes - along the planes they lie on, and by their ends to planes crossing there - so a detail item's arrow stretches with its length.

ALIGNS AND LOCKS a family's 2D LINES to named reference planes, so they stretch when a labelled dimension moves the planes - detail lines and symbolic lines already drawn, and the edges of a FILLED REGION's sketch. What is done by hand with Align, the plane, the line or its end, the padlock. The step that makes a detail item's flow arrow grow with its Length. **TWO KINDS OF LOCK.** ALONG: a straight line lying ON a plane named is locked along it. AT AN END: a line's END lying on a plane that CROSSES the line is locked to it, so the end goes where the plane goes. That is what makes a SLANTED line - an arrow head's edge - follow: its ends are locked to the head-base and tip planes, and it re-draws between them. **AN ARC'S CENTRE (version 3, 2026-11-12).** An arc - or a whole circle - drawn as a detail or symbolic line whose CENTRE lies on a plane named is locked there by its centre, so a symbol's circle stays on its planes when a size moves them; LABEL_FAMILY_RADIUS labels how big it is. Revit gives no centre to lock while the arc's Center Mark is hidden, so the mark is switched on first and said. A whole circle has no ends and is taken for its centre alone; an ellipse or a spline is refused. **A FILLED REGION'S CORNERS ONCE.** Its edges are joined at the corners, so each corner is locked once per plane, and not to a plane an edge through it is already locked along. Loose detail and symbolic lines are separate, so every end is locked on its own. **WHICH LINES**: by id (commas between - the ids DRAW_FAMILY_DETAIL_LINES and DRAW_FAMILY_FILLED_REGION gave back), `selected` in the family's window, or `all` - every detail line, symbolic line and filled region in the family. A form's own sketch is refused, naming LOCK_FORM_SKETCH_TO_PLANES. **LOCKED ONLY WHERE IT ALREADY LIES.** A plane named that nothing lies along and nothing ends on refuses the WHOLE call, naming the nearest ends and how far off - a lock never moves what it locks. A plane not seen edge on in the lines' view is refused. A lock already there is left as it is and said, so a second run adds only what is new. Ends on no plane named are counted and said: they stay put when the planes move. **ONE PLANE PER PLACE**, as DRAW_FAMILY_DETAIL_LINES rules it: of planes named that coincide, the one that does not define the origin is locked to; two such are refused as ambiguous, never both locked. A plane that touches a line in a view where it is not seen edge on refuses the whole call - lock each view's lines in a call of their own. **ALL OR NOTHING, READ BACK.** Every lock reads back locked, and every line's ends read back exactly where they were; any refusal from Revit fails the call with nothing kept. The ends come back in `ends`. Locked is not yet proved to FOLLOW: change the length in Family Types and run this again - every lock said as already there, and `ends` read where the planes now are. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="lock-form-sketch-to-planes"></a>

### Lock form sketch to planes

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-10 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** align and lock the lines and circle centres of a family form's sketch - a sweep's path, an extrusion's circle - to the named planes they lie on.

ALIGNS AND LOCKS the SKETCH a form is drawn from to named reference planes and levels in the family open in the Family Editor - what is done by hand in Edit Sweep > Edit Path or Edit Extrusion: Align, the plane, the sketch line or the circle's centre, the padlock. A sweep's path lines follow the planes so the sweep is rebuilt where they move; a round spigot's circle stays centred when the box around it changes size. **THE SKETCH, NOT THE FACES.** LOCK_FORM_TO_PLANES locks the finished form's faces. On a sweep that was measured to stop every later size change ("Constraints are not satisfied", "Can't create sweep" - Revit 2020, 2026-11-10), because a sweep is rebuilt from its path; and a circle has no flat face at its centre. So for a sweep's path, and for any circle's centre, the lock goes in the sketch. **WHAT IS LOCKED, FOR EACH PLANE NAMED**: every straight sketch line lying in it, both ends on it; and every circle or arc whose centre lies on it, once per centre - Revit keeps a sketch circle as two half-arcs, and one half's centre carries the circle. The sketch is an extrusion's or revolve's own, a sweep's or swept blend's PATH, a blend's base and top; a sweep's profile is not touched. An arc whose centre gives no reference is given "Center Mark Visible" first, as by hand, and that is said. **LOCKED ONLY WHERE IT ALREADY LIES.** A plane with no line and no centre on it refuses the whole call, naming the nearest ones and how far off - a lock never moves what it locks. A plane that does not stand square to the sketch is refused - naming LOCK_FORM_TO_PLANES for an extrusion's or blend's end or top, but never for a sweep, whose ends follow its path. A lock already there is left as it is and said, so a second run adds only what is new. **A CIRCLE'S SIZE IS LABELLED FIRST.** A locked centre moves the circle, but a circle with no size label stretches as it moves - one edge stays where it was. Measured 2026-11-10 (Revit 2020, NEEDS-CHECKING NA5): with no label the centre reached (250, 50) and the circle read 350 across instead of 150; with its diameter labelled by LABEL_FAMILY_RADIUS it moved whole, 150 across. So LABEL_FAMILY_RADIUS first, then this. **THE FORM IS NAMED BY ITS ID** - the one its form tool gave back - or SELECTED in the family's window and called `selected`. Exactly one. **ALL OR NOTHING, READ BACK.** Every lock reads back locked, and the form must still be a solid that has not moved; any refusal from Revit fails the call with nothing kept. Locks already on the form's own faces are counted and said, never removed. Locked is not yet proved to FOLLOW: FLEX_FAMILY moves the planes and reads the form back. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="lock-form-to-planes"></a>

### Lock form to planes

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-18 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** align and lock the flat faces of a family form to the named planes they lie on.

ALIGNS AND LOCKS a form's flat faces to named reference planes and levels in the family open in the Family Editor - the closed padlock after Align - so the form follows the planes when a labelled dimension moves them. Any form: an extrusion of any shape, a blend, the flat ends of a revolve or a sweep. The step that makes a form parametric; EXTRUDE_BETWEEN_PLANES does it for its own boxes, and this is every other form. **A FACE IS LOCKED ONLY WHERE IT ALREADY LIES.** The alignment call's own remarks: the two references must already be aligned, and the call will not force them. So for each plane named, every flat face of the form lying precisely on it is locked, and a plane with no face on it refuses the whole call, naming where the faces facing that way lie, or how far off they are. **IN THE VIEW THAT SEES THE FACE EDGE ON**, as it is done by hand: a face facing left-right or front-back in a floor plan, one facing up or down in an elevation. A face Revit gives no reference for is named, not skipped - reported from an earlier family build for a form sketched on a vertical plane. **THE FORM IS NAMED BY ITS ID** - the one its form tool gave back - or SELECTED in the family's window and called `selected`. Exactly one. **ALL OR NOTHING, READ BACK.** After the locks the form's extent must not have moved - a lock never moves what it locks - and any refusal from Revit fails the call with nothing kept. Locked is not yet proved to FOLLOW: FLEX_FAMILY moves the planes and reads the form back. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="lock-nested-family-to-planes"></a>

### Lock nested family to planes

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-11 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** align and lock a nested family's own reference planes to the planes of the family it sits in.

ALIGNS AND LOCKS a nested family to the planes of the family it sits in - the padlock after Align - so it follows the planes a labelled dimension moves instead of staying where it was dropped. **ITS SIDES ARE ITS OWN PLANES' IS REFERENCE** - Left, Right, Front, Back, Top, Bottom and the three centres - which are the only planes a nested component shows to the family around it. A side it does not have is refused with the sides it does; SET_FAMILY_PLANE_REFERENCE, run in the nested family, gives a plane one. **A SIDE IS LOCKED ONLY TO A PLANE IT ALREADY LIES ON** - Revit's own rule for the alignment call. A side turned the other way is refused before anything is locked; Revit refuses the rest by its own words. **THE LOCKS ARE PAIRS**, nested side = this family's plane or level, semicolons between. The nested component is named by its id, or SELECTED and called `selected`. **AN ARRAY'S COPY TOO** (version 2, 2026-10-07): every array member is a model group, and ARRAY_FAMILY_FORMS gives back the groups' ids; a group holding exactly one nested family is locked through it. Measured on a scratch family: the last copy of a row spread to its last member, its Top locked to a plane, re-spaced the row when the plane moved; the second copy of a row stepped member by member was refused by Revit. Proved again 2026-10-07 on scratch SpringProof, signed by Ajmal PS. **A DETAIL ITEM TOO** (version 3, 2026-11-11): a view-based nested family - a detail item placed in the family's plan, like a diffuser's flow arrows - is locked in the view it is drawn in, as Align is used on it by hand, and only to a plane seen edge-on there: a level, or any plane lying flat in that view, is refused before anything is locked. **ONE WITH NO VIEW OF ITS OWN TOO** (version 4, 2026-11-11): a detail item placed by PLACE_FAMILY_INSTANCES sits on a level's plane and belongs to no view, so it is known by its category, Detail Items, or its family's View Based placement, and locked in the floor plan of the level it sits on - any floor plan when none is of that level - or, standing on a vertical plane, in an elevation looking at it: where Align is used on it by hand. **ALL OR NOTHING, READ BACK**: a lock never moves what it locks, so the nested family's extent is read before and after, and any move fails the call. A detail item has no extent outside its view, so it is read back by its insertion point and, where Revit gives one, its box in its own view. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="open-family-for-editing"></a>

### Open family for editing

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-16 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** put a loaded family in front in Revit, so it can be worked on.

Opens a loaded family in Revit's OWN WINDOW and makes it the document in front, so anything that writes to the active family can then reach it. **IT EXISTS BECAUSE EditFamily OPENS A FAMILY NOBODY CAN SEE.** A document from EditFamily is real and editable, and it is invisible: it never becomes the window in front, and it cannot be loaded back into the project without an answer to Revit's overwrite question that a fragment is not allowed to give. Edit such a document and close it and the work goes with it - measured on 2026-09-16, six families imported and every import discarded. **SO IT GOES THROUGH A FILE, DELIBERATELY.** The family is saved to a .rfa and that file is opened in the UI. A document opened this way is a window a person can see, work in, and LOAD INTO PROJECT from - which is the step the API route could not reach. The file is the bridge, not a side effect. **IT CHANGES NOTHING IN THE PROJECT.** No family is loaded, no element is touched. It writes one .rfa and opens a window. What happens in that window afterwards is somebody else's fragment, and loading it back is a person's click. **THE FAMILY IN FRONT AFTERWARDS IS NOT THE PROJECT'S COPY.** It is the file just written, which starts identical to it. Until it is loaded back, the project still holds the original - so a change made in that window has not reached the model, and saying otherwise would be the same lie the API route told. **IT CANNOT RUN INSIDE A TRANSACTION.** Both EditFamily and OpenAndActivateDocument refuse while the document is modifiable - "The document is currently modifiable! Close the transaction before calling EditFamily." That is why this is EXECUTE rather than MODIFY: it must be sent without the executor opening one. **VERSION 2: THE SAME CODE, AND THE SWITCH THAT SAYS WHAT IT NEEDS** - `noTransactionOpen` (D-125), as `OPEN_VIEW` declared it at its version 3. Version 1 declared nothing, so once its own door had gone it had none that could run it: `revit_show` turns it away because it writes a .rfa (row 5b-591), and `revit_change` ran it inside a transaction, which EditFamily refused - *"The document is currently modifiable! Close the transaction before calling EditFamily."* - seen on Revit 2024, `villa 2`, 2026-11-11 (row 5b-1701, issue #853). With the switch, `revit_change` runs it inside the job's group with no transaction open. `impl/` did not move, so its proof stands. **THAT PROOF WAS NOT TAKEN INSIDE A GROUP**: whether EditFamily and OpenAndActivateDocument run there is NEEDS-CHECKING Group NY's NY3, so a PROVEN line speaks for this code, not yet for that route. **VERSION 3 (2026-11-16): WHAT IS IN FRONT IS READ BACK, NOT TAKEN FROM REVIT'S ANSWER** (row 5b-1820, repairing row 5b-1750 - issue #853). NY3 answered on Revit 2024, `ny-scratch`, through `revit_change`: OpenAndActivateDocument, called inside the job's group, threw "An internal error has occurred." - and the family window WAS open and in front (Revit's title bar read "M_Single-Flush - Floor Plan: Ground floor", and the next call was pinned to it). Version 2 reported `opened false` and that sentence as its `problem`, so the chat said STOPPED over a family that had opened. Now, after a throw or no window handed back, the document in front is read: it counts as `opened` only when it is a family document whose file is the .rfa just written and no window on that file was open before the run - a window left from an earlier run into the same folder has the same path - and Revit's words go into `findings`, not `problem`. A family open but NOT in front is said apart, and stays `opened false` with its `problem` - the next fragment writes to whatever is in front. `impl/` moved, so the card is DRAFT again; the proof below is version 1's record, kept, and NEEDS-CHECKING Group OD proves this one.

<a id="place-adaptive-points"></a>

### Place adaptive points

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-23 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** place the adaptive points an adaptive component is clicked into place by, in an adaptive or pattern-based family.

Places POINTS in an adaptive component, a pattern-based panel or a mass open in the Family Editor - the Point tool, then Make Adaptive. A modeller places an adaptive family by clicking its PLACEMENT points in their number order, and its shape follows wherever they land: a four-point panel, a two-point beam, a three-point bracket. A SHAPE HANDLE point moves the shape after placement; a plain REFERENCE point is a point to build on. **ONLY IN A CONCEPTUAL FAMILY.** Revit makes reference points only in an adaptive component, a pattern-based panel or a mass; any other family is refused before anything is made, naming the templates that make one. A PLACEMENT or SHAPE HANDLE point is an adaptive point, which Revit makes only in an adaptive family - a mass is refused them and takes reference points. **THREE WAYS TO SAY WHERE**, semicolons between, made in the order given: FREE - "X,Y,Z" in millimetres from the family origin; HOSTED ON A LINE - "on <line id> at 0.25", that far along it from its start (Revit's normalised curve parameter), so it slides with the line: an inset frame, a mid-point, an opening that scales with the cell; HOSTED ON A POINT'S OWN PLANE - "on point 1 yz 0,150", millimetres along that plane's two axes, so a profile drawn through such points turns with the point: a two-point beam's section. A hosted point is a REFERENCE point that follows its host; placement and shape handle points are free ones, so the two are not mixed in one call. **PUSHED OFF A POINT'S PLANE (version 2)** - Revit's Offset: "on point 7 normal 300" puts a point 300 mm off the plane of point 7 that lies in the panel, along the panel's normal - a folded panel's TIP over a centre point, so lines from the corners to it make a pyramid facet; "on point 1 xy 0,0 offset 300" pushes off a plane named. Offset reads the number typed, and the answer says which side of the panel that is; a negative number is the other side. Its Offset can then follow a family parameter such as Tip Depth through LINK_FAMILY_PARAMETER. **ALL OR NOTHING**: every point's position, kind and number are read again; placement numbers must rise in the order given, and numbers that are not the next ones after the family's own are reported. A point where another already is - in this call or in the family - is refused. Their ids come back. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="remove-family-connector"></a>

### Remove family connector

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-18 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** delete a connector from the family being edited - named by the plane its face lies on, its id, or all.

Deletes connectors from the family open in the Family Editor - a connector ADD_FAMILY_CONNECTOR put on the wrong face, or one the family no longer needs - the way selecting it and pressing Delete does. **A CONNECTOR IS NAMED THE WAY SET_FAMILY_CONNECTOR_ROLES NAMES ONE** - by the plane its face lies on, "Air Outlet", by the id REPORT_FAMILY_CONNECTORS gives it, or "all"; commas between several. A plane holding more than one connector is refused with their ids, so the wrong one is never deleted, and a name that finds nothing is refused with the family's connectors listed - never guessed. **ALL OR NOTHING.** Every name is checked before the first connector goes. Each is then deleted and read back gone; one that is still there, or a connector that was NOT named going with them, fails the call with nothing kept. Anything else Revit deleted along with them is listed by id. **WHAT IS LEFT BEHIND IS SAID.** The family parameters that drove a connector's size stay in the family (DELETE_FAMILY_PARAMETERS removes them); a connector it was linked to is read back unlinked; a domain left with no PRIMARY connector is named, with the SET_FAMILY_CONNECTOR_ROLES words that set one. The connectors left are listed after. **A PROJECT IN FRONT IS REFUSED** - a placed element's connectors belong to its family, and are deleted there. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="report-family-connectors"></a>

### Report family connectors

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** what connectors this open family has, where each points, its system, size and flow, whether its Allow Slope Adjustments and Utility boxes are ticked, its angle, preset flow and electrical values.

Lists every connector of the family open in the Family Editor, with nothing selected: its domain, System Classification, its size and the family parameters driving it, Flow Direction and Flow Configuration, which way it points - "right (+X)" - where it sits in millimetres, and the plane its face lies on. **THE PLANE IS ITS NAME.** ADD_FAMILY_CONNECTOR places a connector on the face lying on a named plane, and SET_FAMILY_CONNECTOR_ROLES finds it by that plane again - "Port Left". Two connectors on one plane are named, so they can be given by id instead. **READ BEFORE CHANGING.** A port left pointing into the body after its face moved, or a valve port still Domestic Cold Water rather than Global, shows here. REPORT_CONNECTORS is for placed elements in a project. **VERSION 2 (2026-10-22).** The tick boxes and the other typed values that SET_FAMILY_CONNECTOR_ROLES version 4 sets are read here too, so they can be read back without a write: a pipe connector's Allow Slope Adjustments either way ("slope adjustments allowed" / "no slope adjustments"), Utility where ticked, a fitting connector's Angle, a preset Flow, a System flow's Flow Factor, and an electrical connector's Voltage, Number of Poles, Apparent Load, Power Factor, Power Factor State and Load Classification. **ONE LINE**, as REPORT_FAMILY_FORMS answers: a list is cut to three entries before anyone reads it. It reads only; nothing is changed.

<a id="report-family-forms"></a>

### Report family forms

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-23 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** what forms this open family is modelled from, with their ids, sizes and settings - and those forms picked by id or kind, ready to select or delete.

Lists the FORMS a family is made of - every extrusion, revolve, blend, sweep and swept blend in the family open in the Family Editor, solid or void, with its id, its plane, its extent in millimetres, a solid's volume, its subcategory, where it shows, and the cut or join it is in. Read before locking, labelling, cutting or hiding forms. **THE ONLY WAY TO NAME A FORM MADE BY HAND** - the form tools give back their forms' ids, and one drawn by hand has none until this reads it. **ONE LINE**, as REPORT_FAMILY_PARAMETERS answers: a list is cut to three entries before anyone reads it. **COUNT AND EXTENTS FIRST, EACH FORM ONCE, AND NO MORE THAN 60 DESCRIBED (version 6, 2026-11-20)** - past 60, the rest are one line of ids, to be read by those ids or by a kind or a side; every form is still handed on. **`which` NARROWS IT** - "all", or kinds and sides with commas between: "void", "solid, revolve", "swept blend", "freeform" - or the ids the form tools gave back, commas between, to read just those forms, one form's extents after a flex. Ids and words are not mixed; an id that is not a form of this family is refused by name and nothing is read. **AND IT HANDS THEM ON (version 4, 2026-11-01).** SELECT_FAMILY_FORMS, which picked forms by the same ids and kinds, was merged into this card and is DEPRECATED. The forms read are left as `elements`, in the order their ids were named: SET_SELECTION highlights them, DELETE_ELEMENTS deletes them, and any tool that takes elements works on them. One id that is not a form here refuses the whole call and hands NOTHING on, so a delete after it can never reach part of a list. Left out, `which` reads every form and hands none on - a delete needs the forms named, or "all" said. **AND THE FAMILY'S 2D SIDE (version 5, 2026-11-11)** - every DETAIL LINE, SYMBOLIC LINE, FILLED and MASKING REGION and NESTED FAMILY, in `twoDList`: its view or plane, ends in millimetres (an arc's centre and radius), line style or region type, a symbolic line's detail levels and kinds of view, its Visible and what that is linked to, a nested family's type, point, rotation, mirror and linked parameters - and WHAT HOLDS EACH ONE, every dimension and alignment referencing it in words: "locked along Head Top", "locked at an end to Tip", "labelled Length to ...", "EQ with ...". A region's sketch edges are counted under it, never listed as loose lines. `which` takes "2d", "detail line", "symbolic line", "line", "filled region", "masking region", "region" or "nested" - "2d" takes a nested family only when it is 2D itself, a detail item or an annotation, so a delete chained after it never reaches a nested 3D part - and the 2D tools' ids among the forms'. Form words alone read no 2D; 2D words alone read no form. A 2D element is handed on as `elements` only when named by a 2D kind or by id - "all" hands on forms alone, so a delete chained after it never reaches a line. A region's edge named by id is refused, naming the region: its edges are read under it, never handed on alone. Revit giving no edges for a region, or a dimension that cannot be read, is said in a finding. It reads only; nothing is changed.

<a id="report-family-labels"></a>

### Report family labels

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-22 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** every label in the tag, annotation or title block family open in the Family Editor - where it is, its type, width and alignment, and on Revit 2027 the parameters it shows in order with each one's sample value, prefix, suffix, spaces, break and unit format.

Lists every label in the family open in the Family Editor - a tag, a generic annotation, a title block, any category - with where it sits in millimetres, its view, its label type and the label types it can take, its width, horizontal and vertical alignment, angle, Keep Readable, what its Visible is linked to, and the text Revit gives for it. labelContains narrows the list. Text notes are counted and left out: they are not labels. **WHICH PARAMETERS A LABEL SHOWS, AND HOW - REVIT 2027 ONLY.** On 2027 each label's parameters come back in the label's order: the parameter's name and whether it is built-in, shared with its GUID or the family's own, its sample value, prefix, suffix, spaces before it, whether it starts a new line, and its unit format - units, rounding, symbol, + sign, digit grouping, as a Bottom Elevation label in millimetres with the + sign shows it - as Revit returns it for that label. Revit 2020 to 2026 have no way to read those, and the answer says so rather than guessing from the text. **IT NEVER CHANGES A LABEL.** Run it before moving, sizing or copying one.

<a id="report-family-parameters"></a>

### Report family parameters

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-14 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** what parameters this open family has, and what the current type sets them to.

Lists the parameters of the family open for editing - name, storage type, whether it is an instance or a type parameter, any formula, and what the current type sets it to. The question asked before changing anything inside a family. **IT IS THE ANSWER TO "WHERE DOES THIS FAMILY GET ITS MATERIAL".** A fitting family usually carries a MATERIAL PARAMETER, and its geometry is tied to that rather than to a material directly - so the project can drive it per type. Painting a material onto the geometry instead hard-codes it, and the family can then never be anything else. Which of the two a family does is not visible from outside it, and getting it wrong is not a small mistake, so it is read before it is changed. **A FORMULA MEANS THE VALUE IS NOT YOURS TO SET.** A parameter driven by a formula refuses a written value, and the refusal reads like a failure of the write rather than a fact about the parameter. So the formula is reported beside the value. **EVERY PARAMETER COMES BACK AS ONE STRING.** A list is abbreviated to its first three entries before a reader sees it, and a family with forty parameters then reads as though it had three. **IT NEEDS THE FAMILY OPEN FOR EDITING.** Parameters belong to the family document. Run it with a project in front and it says so rather than reporting nothing, because "no parameters" and "you are looking at the wrong document" are different answers. Changes nothing and opens no transaction.

<a id="report-family-tables-in-project"></a>

### Report family tables in project

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** what sizes a family's lookup tables actually hold - the family in front read row by row, or every loaded family from the project without opening any by hand.

Opens each loaded family from the PROJECT, reads its lookup tables, writes them out as CSV, and closes it again - so a whole set of fittings can be checked in one pass instead of one family at a time by hand. **OR THE FAMILY IN FRONT, ROW BY ROW (version 2, 2026-11-01).** REPORT_FAMILY_SIZE_TABLE, which read the lookup table of the family open in the Family Editor, was merged into this card and is DEPRECATED. With a family in front this reads it directly: every table it holds named in `tableNames`, and one table whole - every row in `rows`, the column headers, Revit's own value strings - `tableName` picking it, empty reading the first, and a name the family has not got refused with the ones it has, never a silent fall back. `exportTo` writes that table as CSV. From a project, when `nameContains` narrows to ONE family, its table is read whole the same way. It answers "why does this fitting not appear at my size": a size missing from the lookup table is silent - Revit inserts nothing, or the wrong geometry, and says nothing either way. **IT EXISTS BECAUSE A SIZE TABLE IS ONLY REACHABLE FROM INSIDE THE FAMILY.** Reading the family in front means opening each one, looking, and closing it. A pipe type references eight fitting families, and every one of them can carry the same stale table - so doing it by hand is eight rounds of the same work and the easiest place to stop early. **IT CHANGES NOTHING AND KEEPS NOTHING OPEN.** Each family document is closed WITHOUT saving the moment its tables are read. A family left open is not a neutral side effect: the next fragment would find it in front and answer about the wrong document. **A FAMILY THAT REFUSES TO OPEN IS NAMED, NOT SKIPPED.** In-place families and some system families cannot be edited, and a silent skip is indistinguishable from a family with no table. Both are real answers and they are different ones. **THE CSV IS THE POINT, NOT THE SUMMARY.** Tables are wide - a reducing tee is two keys and three dimensions - and no line of text holds one. The summary says which family has which table and how many rows; the files hold what is actually in them.

<a id="report-family-template"></a>

### Report family template

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-24 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** what kind of family is open - wall, ceiling, floor, roof or face based, line based, adaptive, pattern based, profile, detail or annotation - what its template already holds, and its OmniClass Number and the codes that fit its category.

Says what KIND of family is open in the Family Editor, and what its template already holds, before anything is built in it: level-based, work-plane-based, face-based, wall-, ceiling-, floor- or roof-based, line-based, a line-based or ordinary detail item, an adaptive component, a pattern-based curtain panel or a classic curtain wall panel - told apart by the reference points only the pattern-based one can hold - a conceptual mass, a profile, an annotation or a title block. **THE TEMPLATE DECIDED IT AND NOTHING CHANGES IT.** A wall-based family cannot become a face-based one, a line-based family takes its Length from two clicks, a pattern-based panel is driven by its tile pattern's points. The method that builds each kind differs, so the kind is READ - from the family's own placement, its category, Revit's own flags and the host element the template carries - never guessed from the name. **WITH WHAT IS ALREADY THERE**, each on ONE line: the named reference planes, where each sits, what it faces, its Is Reference and Defines Origin; the host wall, ceiling, floor or roof; the built-in parameters with their values - a line-based family's Length, a door's Width and Height; the family's own switches, Host, Part Type, Profile Usage and a structural family's Material for Model Behavior and Section Shape among them; the reference lines and the lines drawn through points, with their ids; the adaptive points with their placement numbers, ids and Orientation; a pattern panel's tile pattern and spacing; the views; the types. It reads only; nothing is changed. **VERSION 2 (2026-10-11): THE OMNICLASS NUMBER AND TITLE** join the settings (Classification Number and Title from Revit 2026), and it lists the codes the classification file gives this family's category - what a family build proposes the code from - or says why there are none.

<a id="report-family-type-catalog"></a>

### Report family type catalog

**DRAFT - runs in a chat, and its answer says so.** It changes nothing in the model, so it is not refused, but it has not been proved on a real model yet.

**What it does:** write this family's types as a type catalog - the .txt beside the family that makes Revit ask which types to load.

Reads every type of the family open in the Family Editor and gives back a TYPE CATALOG - the text file, with the family's name and .txt, kept beside the .rfa, that makes Revit show "Specify Types" when the family is loaded, so a project takes the five sizes it needs out of fifty. The header line starts with the delimiter and names each column "Name##KIND##UNIT"; each next line is a type and its values. **THE HEADER WORDS ARE REVIT'S, NEVER TYPED HERE.** Each column's kind and unit come from Revit's own "string used in type catalogs" for the parameter's kind and for the unit the family displays it in - Revit renamed some unit words in 2021, which is why they are asked for rather than written down. **WHAT IS LEFT OUT IS SAID**: instance parameters, values a formula or a dimension drives, values holding an element - a material, a nested type - and a parameter blank in every type, each named. **IT WRITES NOTHING.** The text and the file name come back; the family's own path with .txt when it has been saved. It reads only; nothing is changed.

<a id="report-nested-families"></a>

### Report nested families

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-09 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** how many whole units are these, not how many family instances.

Groups elements by the whole piece of kit they belong to - walking UP to the outermost host and DOWN to every nested part - and says how far a plain instance count is from the number of real units. Read-only. **A COUNT OF NESTED EQUIPMENT IS NOT A COUNT OF EQUIPMENT.** An air handling unit with a nested fan, coil and filter is four family instances in the same category. Every schedule, and every count this library can make, returns four. There is one unit on site. The same happens to a pump set, a packaged chiller, a valve set, a light fitting with a nested emergency module - and it is invisible, because four is a perfectly plausible number. **INSULATION AND LINING ARE THE SAME PROBLEM IN DIFFERENT CLOTHES.** They are separate elements that belong to a host and inflate a count exactly as a nested part does. They are followed through the host relationship, so a lagged pipe is one unit rather than three. **THE WALK GOES BOTH WAYS, AND UP IS THE ONE THAT WAS MISSING.** Walking down from a host is the easy direction and it answers the wrong question: a category filter catches the nested FAN, not the AHU it sits in, because a nested part can be in a different category from its host. Asking each element for its host and following that to the top is what puts the fan back with its unit - and where that host is not in the set it was given, its id is named in `rootsOutsideSet`, because that is the filter's blind spot made visible. **THE WALK IS GUARDED AGAINST A CYCLE.** Nothing should be its own ancestor, and a corrupt or half-copied family has produced one. An unguarded loop on the host relationship hangs Revit rather than erroring, so every id visited is remembered and a repeat stops the walk and names the element. **IT REPORTS THE NESTING; IT DOES NOT JUDGE IT.** A shared nested family is a real independent instance by design - it is meant to schedule and tag on its own. The difference between the instance count and the unit count is the flag to look at, not the verdict. ASSUMES NOTHING ABOUT TRANSACTIONS - it opens none and needs none.

| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |

<a id="set-adaptive-point-orientation"></a>

### Set adaptive point orientation

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** set the Orientation of an adaptive component's points - Instance, Host, Host and Loop System or Global - in the adaptive family being edited.

Sets the ORIENTATION of an adaptive component's points, in the family open in the Family Editor - the Orientation row Properties shows for each point: Instance (xyz), Revit's default; Instance (z) then Host (xy); Host (xyz); Host and Loop System (xyz), what a panel on a surface usually needs; Global (xyz); Global (z) then Host (xy). It decides which way each point's planes turn once the family is in a project. **WHICH POINTS**: all of them, or by number - "1,2,4" or "1-4". A shape handle point is listed and left: Revit's API sets an orientation on placement points only. **ONLY IN AN ADAPTIVE COMPONENT** - a project or any other family is refused by name before anything is written. **READ BACK, ALL OR NOTHING**: a point already as asked is counted and left; every adaptive point is read again after the write, and one that does not read as asked - or one not asked for that moved - fails the call. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="set-divided-surface-layout"></a>

### Set divided surface layout

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-23 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** change how a divided surface already there is laid out - its U and V grids, their rotation, offset and justification, the border tiles, the component flip, and the levels or planes that cut it.

CHANGES A DIVIDED SURFACE THAT IS ALREADY THERE, in a mass or pattern-based family open in the Family Editor - the settings its Properties list under U Grid and V Grid and for the surface itself. DIVIDE_FAMILY_SURFACE divides a face; this changes the divided surface afterwards, without dividing it again. **ONE DIVIDED SURFACE**, by the id DIVIDE_FAMILY_SURFACE or REPORT_DIVIDED_SURFACES gave, or the only one in the family when none is named. With several and none named, nothing changes and their ids are listed. **THE REQUEST IS A SHORT TABLE**, semicolons between - "all rotation=45" to rotate the grid 45 degrees for a diamond pattern, "u layout=number; u number=20" for 20 divisions, "v layout=distance; v distance=1500", "u offset=750", "u justification=center", "border=empty" for empty border tiles, "flip=yes" to flip the panels, "intersect=levels" to divide the surface at every level. Only what is named changes; every other setting is left as it was. Each grid takes a layout (none, number, distance, maximum spacing, minimum spacing), its number or distance, a justification (center, beginning, end), a rotation and an offset. The surface takes all rotation, border (empty, partial, overhanging), component rotation (0, 90, 180 or 270), flip, mirror, u indent and v indent, and intersect - levels, reference planes, or levels and planes by name - which cuts the surface where each crosses it; "none" removes every cut. **MILLIMETRES AND DEGREES.** A distance is 100 to 100,000 mm and an offset 0 or 10 to 100,000 mm either way, so 1.5 typed as metres is refused rather than laid out every 1.5 mm. An angle is -360 to 360 degrees. **ALL OR NOTHING.** After the rebuild every setting written is checked against Revit; one that does not hold as written fails the call and nothing is kept. A level or plane Revit says cannot cut the surface is skipped and named. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="set-family-connector-roles"></a>

### Set family connector roles

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-12 (Revit 2020, 2024).

**What it does:** edit a connector already in the family being edited - set its system classification, flow, size parameters, voltage, poles, load and power factor, tick or untick its Allow Slope Adjustments and Utility boxes, set a fitting connector's angle, a preset flow or flow factor, flip it, make it primary, link a pair.

Edits a connector that is ALREADY in the family open in the Family Editor - the settings ADD_FAMILY_CONNECTOR leaves at Revit's defaults, and the ones a modeller changes later: System Classification (Global and Fitting too), Flow Direction, Flow Configuration, Loss Method with its coefficient or pressure drop, Description, the family parameters driving its size, which way it points (a flip), which connector is PRIMARY and which pairs are LINKED - and, from version 3, an ELECTRICAL connector's Voltage, Number of Poles, Apparent Load, Power Factor and Load Classification. **`settings` IS ONE VALUE** - "system=Global; flowDirection=In; flip=true" - holding only what should change, for every connector `connectors` names. Keys: system, flowDirection, flowConfiguration, lossMethod, lossCoefficient, pressureDrop (Pa), description, flip, sizeParameters, utility (yes/no); on a pipe connector allowSlopeAdjustments (yes/no); on a duct or pipe connector flowFactor and presetFlow (L/s); on a fitting's connector angle (degrees); and on an electrical connector voltage, poles, apparentLoad, powerFactor, powerFactorState and loadClassification. **AN ELECTRICAL VALUE IS A NUMBER, A FAMILY PARAMETER, OR BOTH** - "voltage=400 V; poles=3; apparentLoad=1.5 kVA; powerFactor=0.85" sets the values; "voltage=[Voltage]" drives the connector's Voltage from the family parameter Voltage, making it - a type parameter of the field's own kind, under Electrical - Loads, as Revit's Associate Family Parameter dialog does with New Parameter - when the family has none; "voltage=400 V [Voltage]" does both and writes 400 V into the current type. A project schedules a family's value only through a SHARED parameter: add it first with ADD_FAMILY_PARAMETERS, kind shared, and name it in the brackets. Voltage in V or kV, Apparent Load in VA or kVA, Number of Poles 1 to 3 (a three-phase connector is 3), Power Factor above 0 to 1 or a percentage. Revit keeps a voltage and a load in its own internal units; the conversion is checked against Revit's own on the release that runs, and every value is read back with what Revit shows. Load Classification is a classification's name in the family, set as a value only. **VERSION 4 (2026-10-22).** A connector's TICK BOXES and the other typed values its Properties show: "allowSlopeAdjustments=yes" on a PIPE connector - the box a drain family's connectors need ticked before the pipework from them can be given a fall - "utility=yes", a fitting connector's "angle=90", a duct or pipe connector's "flowFactor=0.5" and "presetFlow=12 L/s" (each a value, a [family parameter] or both, as the electrical values are), and an electrical connector's "powerFactorState=Lagging". A KEY ANOTHER DOMAIN'S CONNECTOR HAS NOT GOT IS REFUSED naming the connector and its domain - Allow Slope Adjustments asked of a duct connector changes nothing. Version 4 was proved on Revit 2020 on 2026-10-24 (the proof below). **VERSION 5 (2026-11-11): THE SHAPE, AND A REFERENCE PLANE TO HOST ON** (FRAGMENT-ISSUES rows 5b-1566 and 5b-1567). "shape=Round", Rectangular or Oval changes a DUCT connector's Shape - a connector placed by hand comes in Rectangular, and sizeParameters with one name was refused on it. The shape is written through the connector's Shape parameter, only where that reads the same number as the connector's own shape, and read back; sizeParameters in the same call is counted against the NEW shape, so "shape=Round; sizeParameters=Neck Diameter; system=Supply Air; flowDirection=In; flowConfiguration=Preset; presetFlow=[Designed_Air_Flow]" finishes a connector in ONE call. Where Revit keeps the shape read-only the refusal says so, with the way round. "host=Neck Top" moves a connector onto the REFERENCE PLANE named, with no solid face under it - Revit's Place on Work Plane - so the solid it was made on can be deleted without taking the connector with it. Revit 2023 and later only (ChangeHostReference); on 2020 to 2022 it is refused with the ways round - a thin solid with Visible off, or the modeller places it on the work plane and this card sets the rest by its id. The plane must be square to the way the connector points; it is put back where it sat and pointing the way it pointed, read back. It is NOT locked to planes there (row 5b-1568). Version 5 was PROVED on Revit 2020 on 2026-11-12 (Group NO, NO1 - the shape and its size; NO2, NO3, NO7 and NO8 held as well, row 5b-1577), signed by Ajmal PS; its proof replaced version 4's below. The work-plane host is NOT in that proof - it needs Revit 2023 or later. RUN ON REVIT 2024 the same day, rolled back (NO4, NO5, row 5b-1578): Revit took a reference plane's reference, the connector was put back where it sat, and with it hosted the box could be deleted and the connector stayed - without the host it went with the box. **A CONNECTOR'S VALUES ARE SET BY ID HERE** (row 5b-1569). A connector is named by the id REPORT_FAMILY_CONNECTORS prints, or its UniqueId; SET_PARAMETER_VALUES_BY_ID writes elements found by category or UniqueId and finds no category for a family's connectors. **REVIT DECIDES WHICH SYSTEM A CONNECTOR MAY TAKE.** Each connector is asked (IsSystemClassificationValid) before anything changes, so a system Revit keeps from it is refused with the systems it does take. **A LINKED PAIR PASSES A SYSTEM THROUGH THE FAMILY** - a coil, a pump, a valve body. The sources docs/43 §10 records say it does so only when both connectors are Global, so a linked pair that is not is reported with the setting that fixes it; give "system=Global" in the same call to set it. **A CONNECTOR IS NAMED BY THE PLANE ITS FACE LIES ON** - "Port Left", the way ADD_FAMILY_CONNECTOR places one - by its id, or "all". A plane holding more than one connector is refused with their ids. **NOTHING ASKED CHANGES NOTHING**; REPORT_FAMILY_CONNECTORS is the read. **CHECKED FIRST, READ BACK AFTER, ALL OR NOTHING.** Every setting is read back on every connector named - a flip must point the other way, a size must follow its parameter - and one that differs fails the whole call. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="set-family-form-subcategory"></a>

### Set family form subcategory

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-12 (Revit 2020, 2024).

**What it does:** put family forms, or detail and symbolic lines already drawn, on a subcategory of the family's category, making it if it is new.

Puts forms on a SUBCATEGORY of the family's own category in the family open in the Family Editor - the Subcategory field in Properties - so a project can colour, hide or line-weight that part of the family on its own: the insulation, the hidden parts, the casing, the frame. **A SUBCATEGORY THE FAMILY DOES NOT HAVE YET IS MADE**, under the family's category, and the answer says it was made - Object Styles in the Family Editor is where a modeller makes one by hand. A name that differs only by case from one already there is that one, never a second. "none" puts the forms back on the family's category itself, which Revit's remarks name as the field's other value. **A CATEGORY THAT TAKES NO SUBCATEGORIES IS REFUSED BY NAME**, from Revit's own flag for it, before anything is made. **THE FORMS ARE NAMED BY THEIR IDS** - the ones the form tools gave back, commas between - or SELECTED in the family's window and called `selected`. **READ BACK, ALL OR NOTHING.** Each form's subcategory is read again after it is set, and reported before and after; one that does not read as asked fails the call and nothing is kept - the new subcategory included. **DETAIL AND SYMBOLIC LINES TOO** (version 2, 2026-11-11) - a plan symbol's lines, a detail item's outline, already drawn and named by the ids their draw tools gave back or selected. A line is put on the subcategory by its LINE STYLE, the subcategory's projection style, which is what its Subcategory field sets by hand. A line takes only the styles Revit offers it; a subcategory not among them is refused by name, and a new one made for it is not kept. **"none" WORKS ON REVIT 2020 (row 5b-1571, measured 2026-11-12).** Setting a form's Subcategory to its family's category throws "The input subcategory is illegal" - from a subcategory, and from the category itself - so "none" is written as the Subcategory field's empty id, what "None" in Properties is, and a form already on the category is left as it was and said. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="set-family-form-visibility"></a>

### Set family form visibility

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-12 (Revit 2020, 2024).

**What it does:** set at which coarse, medium or fine level, and in which kinds of project view, a family form or a symbolic line appears.

Sets a family form's VISIBILITY SETTINGS in the family open in the Family Editor - the Visibility Settings dialog there: at which level, and in which kinds of project view, a placed family draws the form. A 3D body hidden in a coarse plan; a small part drawn only at the most precise level. **BOTH LISTS ARE NAMED IN FULL** - levels from coarse, medium and fine, kinds from plan, front and left, either one "all". What is not named is switched OFF, so the call states the whole setting, never half of it. A list naming nothing is refused: a form drawn at no level, or in no plan or elevation, vanishes from them with no trace in the family. There is no switch for 3D, which shows the form at the levels named. **THE FORMS ARE NAMED BY THEIR IDS** - the ones the form tools gave back, commas between - or SELECTED in the family's window and called `selected`. **READ BACK, ALL OR NOTHING.** Each form's setting is read again after it is written, and is reported before and after; one that does not read as asked fails the call and nothing is kept. The Family Editor itself keeps showing every form - this is what a project shows. **SYMBOLIC LINES TOO** (version 2, 2026-11-11) - a plan symbol's lines already drawn, named by the ids DRAW_FAMILY_SYMBOLIC_LINES gave back or selected. A symbolic line's setting is of another kind than a form's, so it is written in the kind the line already reads. Its detail levels are set as a form's; whether its kinds of view can be set is not yet measured, so when they are named they are read back and anything else refuses the call, saying what Revit read. Views "unchanged" - what leaving them out means - sets only a symbolic line's detail levels and keeps its kinds of view. A FORM's kinds of view are still named in full: left out, or "unchanged", the call is refused as version 1 refused it. **DETAIL LINES, FILLED REGIONS AND NESTED FAMILIES ARE REFUSED BY NAME** - Revit's API has no visibility settings for any of them on any release 2020 to 2027; they are set by hand in the Family Editor. **MEASURED 2026-11-12 ON REVIT 2020 (Group NF, NF6b):** a symbolic line's setting is of the ViewSpecific kind and Revit would not take kinds of view on it - asked for "plan", the call is refused saying so and nothing is kept. Its detail levels are set with views "unchanged". ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="set-family-formula"></a>

### Set family formula

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-26 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** drive this family parameter by a formula, or clear its formula.

Gives one parameter of the family open in the Family Editor a FORMULA - "Neck Top = Height + Neck Depth", "Neck Width = Width - 100 mm" - or clears the one it has, which is the Formula column of the Family Types dialog. **A FORMULA NEEDS A TYPE TO HOLD ITS RESULT.** A new family has no type, and Revit refuses a formula there with "There is no valid family type" - reported from an earlier family build, where that refusal also took down the parameters added in the same step. So this refuses until a type exists and names SET_FAMILY_TYPE_VALUES, which makes the first one. **NAMES ARE WRITTEN BARE, SPACES AND ALL.** `Height + Neck Depth` works; `Height + "Neck Depth"` is rejected by Revit as an invalid formula with no word about why - reported from the same build, found only by trying each name alone. A formula that puts one of the family's own parameter names in quotes is refused here with that reason, before Revit is asked. A unit may follow a number - `Height + 60 mm` - and text formulas keep their quoted strings, which are not parameter names. **AN EMPTY FORMULA CLEARS IT**, and the parameter keeps the value the formula last gave it and becomes editable again - the way to type a value into a parameter a formula drove. **A FORMULA OF A PLAIN VALUE LOCKS A SIZE.** `600 mm` greys the parameter out, so a manufacturer's product cannot be dragged to a size it is not made in, and it still labels its dimension. That is a deliberate use, not an error. **REVIT'S WORDS COME BACK WHEN IT REFUSES**, through `refused` - never as a thrown error (version 3) - and nothing is kept. The formula and the value it produces in the current type are read back from the family afterwards - by the parameter's kind (version 2): a whole number for an Integer (a blade count), Yes or No for a Yes/No, the text for a text, and a length or other measured value as Revit shows it. An instance parameter reads the same way: the current type holds its value too. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

| **Proved on Revit** | 2020 |

<a id="set-family-light-source"></a>

### Set family light source

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** define the light source of the lighting fixture family being edited - its shape, distribution, position and aim, and each type's intensity or wattage, colour, light loss factor, dimming and colour filter.

Defines the LIGHT SOURCE of a lighting fixture family open in the Family Editor - the Light Source Definition, where the light source sits and which way it points, and the photometric values in Type Properties - through Revit's LightFamily and LightType. **TWO HALVES, ONE PER CALL.** The FAMILY'S light source, one for every type: the SHAPE light leaves - point, line, rectangle or circle, sizes in millimetres; the DISTRIBUTION - spherical, hemispherical, spot (beam and field angles, tilt) or a photometric web from an IES file on this computer, with its tilt; its POSITION - a point in millimetres or onto a named reference plane; and its AIM - tilted or rotated about the family's X, Y or Z. And EACH TYPE'S values: the initial INTENSITY - lumens, candelas, lux at a distance, or a WATTAGE with its efficacy or its lumens; the initial COLOUR TEMPERATURE in kelvin; the LIGHT LOSS FACTOR, one number or seven; the DIMMING colour shift; the COLOUR FILTER. Revit's reference says type values may be lost when they change in one transaction with the family's light source, and that is what version 1 met on Revit 2020 (5b-1297), so a call asking for both halves is refused with that reason - the family's half first, the types' second. **EVERY FAMILY TYPE (version 2, 5b-1298).** The types are the family's own, each made current before its values are written. A type Revit's lighting API does not list - it listed one light type for two family types on Revit 2020 - is written with it current and must then PROVE it was reached from its own Type Properties; every type not asked for must read as it did. No call on any release makes a light type: a type that cannot be proved reached fails the call, and the refusal gives the hand fix. The family's half cannot be asked for one type of several - every type takes it. **LIGHT SOURCE MUST ALREADY BE TICKED** in Family Category and Parameters - Revit's GetLightFamily refuses a family without it. SET_FAMILY_SETTINGS "Light Source=yes" ticks it, and the refusal says so. **A WATTAGE (BV18).** Revit's reference names a wattage's unit two ways - its constructor "a universal unit value", its properties W and lm/W. It is written as W at lm/W, and Type Properties' own Wattage and Efficacy, out of Revit's internal units, must then read what was asked for every type, or the call fails and nothing is kept. A wattage alone, with no efficacy or lumens, is refused: it says nothing about how much light. **THE LIGHT SOURCE IS MOVED AND AIMED AS AN ELEMENT** - no release has a setter for its transform - and the transform is read again: one that did not go where it was sent fails the call. **READ BACK, AND WHAT TYPE PROPERTIES SHOWS IS THE TEST.** Everything asked is read again through the lighting API and through each type's own Type Properties, and the report gives every light value each type changed holds, with the family's shape, distribution, IES file, tilt, position and aim. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

| **You get** | light report, changed, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2020 |

<a id="set-family-plane-reference"></a>

### Set family plane reference

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-23 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** set Is Reference, Defines Origin and Subcategory on the reference planes of the family being edited.

Sets IS REFERENCE and DEFINES ORIGIN on named reference planes in the family open in the Family Editor - the two rows of a plane's Properties that decide how the family behaves once placed: which of its planes a project can dimension and snap to, and which planes fix its insertion point, the point it is placed by. **WHAT EACH PLANE IS GIVEN** - Left, Right, Front, Back, Top, Bottom or one of the three centres, each held by one plane at a time; Strong or Weak Reference for any other plane a project should reach; Not a Reference for a plane only the build needs. Sides and centres go on planes that face their way - Left on a plane facing left or right, Top on a horizontal one. **ONE ALREADY HELD IS REFUSED**, naming the plane that holds it: what that plane becomes is said in the same call, never decided here. **"origin" MOVES THE ORIGIN** onto a plane, from the one facing the same way that had it, and both are reported. A project's units already placed take the new origin when the family is loaded into it again. **NONE OF REVIT'S NUMBERS IS ASSUMED.** Each value is written and read back in Revit's own words, and one whose words never come back fails the call. Every other plane is read before and after, and anything the call did not ask that moved is put back. **SUBCATEGORY** - which subcategory of Reference Planes a plane is drawn in, and so its colour - is set per plane, or for every plane that is not an outline or centre plane at once. The subcategory must already exist. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="set-family-settings"></a>

### Set family settings

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-23 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** set the family's own Category, Work Plane-Based, Shared, Always Vertical, Room Calculation Point, Cut with Voids When Loaded, Part Type, Profile Usage, Material for Model Behavior, Section Shape, OmniClass Number or Light Source in the family being edited.

Sets the switches in Family Category and Parameters for the family open in the Family Editor: WORK PLANE-BASED - placed on any plane or face and moving with it, the way a family nested in another is best made; SHARED - a nested copy that a project schedules and tags as an element of its own; ALWAYS VERTICAL - a Work Plane-Based family that stays upright on a slope; ROOM CALCULATION POINT; CUT WITH VOIDS WHEN LOADED - its unattached voids cut walls, floors and the rest in a project; MAINTAIN ANNOTATION ORIENTATION - a nested symbol stays readable in plan; ROTATE WITH COMPONENT and KEEP TEXT READABLE for an annotation; ENABLE CUTTING IN VIEWS. **AND FOUR THAT TAKE A NAME**: PART TYPE - Elbow, Tee, Transition, Breaks Into, Damper - which decides how an MEP fitting or accessory behaves and which routing preference group offers it; PROFILE USAGE - Wall Sweep, Mullion, Railing - which decides where a profile family is offered; and for a structural framing or column family MATERIAL FOR MODEL BEHAVIOR - Steel, Concrete, Precast Concrete, Wood, Other - which decides its cutback, shape handles and joins, and SECTION SHAPE, which adds the section's schedulable dimensions. Each is matched to Revit's own list, read from the running Revit, and the words Revit shows are accepted with their spaces and dashes. **ONE VALUE FOR THE WHOLE FAMILY**, not per type. A switch this family's category does not have, or that Revit holds read-only here, is refused by name. **WORK PLANE-BASED IS WRITTEN FIRST**, because Always Vertical belongs to a Work Plane-Based family; anything Revit changes on its own as a result is reported as Revit's. **READ BACK, ALL OR NOTHING**: every switch is read again after the last write. Copies already placed elsewhere take a change when the family is loaded there again. **VERSION 2 (2026-10-11): THE OMNICLASS NUMBER** - Classification Number from Revit 2026 - the one setting that takes text. Only a code the classification file files under this family's category is written, and any other is refused with the codes that file gives the category; blank, none or clear empties it. **VERSION 3 (2026-10-21): LIGHT SOURCE** - "Light Source=yes" ticks the box a Lighting Fixtures family needs before SET_FAMILY_LIGHT_SOURCE can define its light, done by hand until then. The switch Revit hands the API is not named Light Source in its reference, so the tick is PROVED: after the write, Revit's lighting API must find a light source in the family, or the call fails and nothing is kept. Only yes is taken - unticking removes the light source and every photometric value, and is left to the modeller. **VERSION 4 (2026-11-01): THE CATEGORY** - SET_FAMILY_CATEGORY's job, merged here: "Category=Air Terminals" makes a family started from a generic template an Air Terminal or Mechanical Equipment. THE FIRST STEP OF BUILDING A FAMILY, AND THE ONE THAT CANNOT WAIT: the category decides which built-in parameters the family carries, which schedules it lands in and which connectors make sense on it, and switching it adds that category's own parameters - `parametersGained`, read from the family, because that is the part people do not expect. The name is matched to the names Revit shows in Family Category and Parameters, in the language it runs in, and NEVER GUESSED - "Air Terminal" is refused with "Air Terminals" offered (D-33). Revit decides which categories a family may take; when it refuses, its own words are passed on and nothing is kept. IN A COMBINED CALL THE CATEGORY IS WRITTEN FIRST, because Part Type, the OmniClass Number and which switches the family has at all are checked against it; once it is written, a problem with any other setting fails the whole call rather than keeping the category alone. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="set-family-sweep-profile"></a>

### Set family sweep profile

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-03 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** draw a family sweep with a loaded profile family instead of a sketched shape, flipped or not.

Sets the PROFILE of one or more sweeps in the family open in the Family Editor to a PROFILE FAMILY loaded into it - the sweep's Profile in its Properties - instead of a shape sketched in place: a handrail's section, a skirting, a gasket, an insulation ring. One profile then serves many sweeps, a change to it reaches them all when it is loaded again, and a Family Type parameter can swap it per type (ADD_FAMILY_TYPE_PARAMETER). **THE SWEEPS ARE NAMED BY ID** - the id a CREATE_FAMILY_FORMS kind=sweep row gives back in formIds (CREATE_FAMILY_SWEEP's formId until 2026-11-01) or REPORT_FAMILY_FORMS reads. A swept blend has two profiles and is refused by name rather than half set. **THE PROFILE IS A TYPE OF A PROFILE FAMILY LOADED HERE**, "Family : Type", or its type name when unique; a name not loaded is refused with the profiles the family holds - LOAD_FAMILY first. A Profile Revit holds read-only is refused, never forced. **READ BACK, ALL OR NOTHING**: each sweep's Profile, its flip, and that it still holds a solid are read again - a profile that does not sweep along the path fails the call. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Changes the model (`MODIFY`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **You say** | **sweeps** - text<br>**profile** - text<br>**flipped** - yes or no - true or false |
| **You get** | changed, profile report, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2024 |

**How to use it**

1. Open the model in Revit and connect Heron: press **Heron** on the Heron tab, so its heron turns orange.
2. Turn **Changes** on in Heron's **Settings** (Heron tab).
3. In a Claude chat, ask in your own words, for example *"use the handrail profile family for this sweep"*. Say the values under **You say** in the same sentence.
4. Heron makes the change as **one entry in Revit's Undo list**. With **Ask to Keep** on, Revit asks **Keep or Discard** first; Ctrl+Z takes it back.

Other ways to ask: *"set the sweep profile to the loaded profile family"* · *"change this sweep to use a profile family"*

<a id="set-family-type-values"></a>

### Set family type values

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-26 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** give this family type these parameter values, making the type if it is new - or rename or delete the family type.

Writes values into one TYPE of the family open in the Family Editor - "600 x 600: Width 600, Depth 600, Height 250" - and makes that type first if the family does not have it yet. What the Family Types dialog does when a type is chosen, or added with New, and its rows are typed in - and what its Rename and Delete do to a family type. **A NEW FAMILY HAS NO TYPE AT ALL**, and several family jobs cannot run without one: a formula needs a current type to hold its result - reported from an earlier family build, where the formula call failed with "There is no valid family type" and took the parameters added beside it down too. So this is the step that makes the first type, and SET_FAMILY_FORMULA refuses until one exists. **UNITS ARE THE PARAMETER'S OWN, written the way a modeller reads them.** A length is millimetres, an angle degrees, a yes/no true or false, a number and an integer as they are, text as typed. The parameter's kind is read from the family, so "Width=600" needs no unit beside it - and "600mm" is refused, because a unit typed into the value is how a length ends up a thousand times wrong. Every other MEASURED kind - an area, an air flow, a volume, a pressure - is read in the family's own units by Revit's own parser, so its unit may be typed ("94.4 L/s") or left out (version 4). A Number of Poles - the electrical spec a shared "Number_of_Poles" holds - is a whole number 1, 2 or 3 (version 6). A kind this does not write at all is refused by name rather than written as something else. **A MATERIAL IS WRITTEN BY ITS NAME** - "Nut Material=Steel - Galvanised" - and only a material the family already holds: the exact name, or the same name in another case when only one material matches. A name the family does not have refuses the whole call, naming the three closest, and no material is ever made. "<By Category>" or "none" clears the parameter back to By Category. A URL, and any other kind Revit keeps as text, is written as text, as typed (version 2 - version 1 refused both). **RENAME OR DELETE A TYPE (version 3).** "Type Name=HexNut - ISO 4032" in the values renames the type `typeName` names, as the dialog's Rename does - only a type that exists, never to a name another type has in any case, never with a character Revit forbids. `deleteType` true removes that type, alone, and never the family's last one. The types are read back after either. **A VALUE A FORMULA DRIVES IS REFUSED, NOT OVERWRITTEN.** Revit will not hold a typed value against a formula, and clearing the formula is a different decision - SET_FAMILY_FORMULA. A reporting parameter is refused for the same reason: its value is read off the geometry. **THIS MOVES GEOMETRY WHEREVER THE PARAMETERS DRIVE IT.** A value written into a parameter that labels a dimension moves those planes, and everything locked to them. That is a flex, and the report counts what each parameter drives so it is never a surprise. Values go in BEFORE a dimension is labelled with a parameter, not after - LABEL_FAMILY_DIMENSION refuses a label whose parameter disagrees with the planes. **ALL OR NOTHING, READ BACK.** Every name and value is checked before the first write; if Revit then refuses one, the call fails and nothing from it is kept. And after the write, every labelled dimension that agreed with its parameter before must still agree: Revit may only WARN about a size its constraints cannot take, and keep the value while the planes stay put - so a dimension that no longer reads its parameter fails the call too. **AND EVERY OTHER MEASURED KIND (version 4, 2026-11-12)** - an air flow, an area, a volume, a pressure: typed with its unit as the Family Types dialog takes it, "94.4 L/s", or as a number in the unit the family shows it in, and read by Revit's own parser in the family's units; read back in Revit's own format. A value Revit cannot read is refused by name, nothing written. **MANY TYPES AT ONCE (version 5).** `typeName` "all" - or a comma list, "600 x 600, 625 x 625" - writes the same values into every type it names in ONE change, one undo entry, and reads every type back: blanking two text values in all seven types is one call, a blank written as empty text. A list writes only types the family has - one name it does not have refuses the whole call, nothing written - and never makes, renames or deletes a type. Revit writes a family type only while it is current, so each type is made current in turn, as the Family Types dialog does, and the type that was current is current again at the end; a type already holding every value is not touched. TEXT into EVERY type - not a URL, which Revit gives no formula - is written with no type made current at all (measured on Revit 2024) - see the compatibility note. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

|---|---|

| **You say** | **type name** - text<br>**values** - name=value, SEMICOLONS between - "view=*-Mech*; sheet=A-*"; a value holding a ";" goes in double quotes - Note="a; b"<br>**delete type** - yes or no - true or false; optional |
| **You get** | type used, type created, written, drives, types written, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2020 |
| **Capability** | `SET_FAMILY_TYPE_VALUES` |

2. Turn **Changes** on in Heron's **Settings** (Heron tab).

4. Heron makes the change as **one entry in Revit's Undo list**. With **Ask to Keep** on, Revit asks **Keep or Discard** first; Ctrl+Z takes it back.

<a id="write-family-size-table"></a>

### Write family size table

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-16 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** replace this family's lookup table with one from a CSV.

Imports a CSV over a family's lookup table - adding the sizes it was missing, or correcting the dimensions it had. The write twin of REPORT_FAMILY_TABLES_IN_PROJECT, which could read a table and say which sizes were absent but never put one right. **A SIZE MISSING FROM THE TABLE IS WHY A FITTING DOES NOT APPEAR**, and it says nothing when it fails. Give a segment new sizes and the family's table is left behind: half the run gets elbows and half gets a bare corner, with no error anywhere. This is how the table catches up. **IT REPLACES, IT DOES NOT MERGE.** Revit's import overwrites the whole table of that name - a CSV holding five rows leaves a table of five rows, not twenty-four. So the CSV must carry EVERY row that is to survive, and the honest way to build one is to export the existing table first and edit that. Reporting `rowsBefore` beside `rowsAfter` is what makes an accidental replacement visible instead of silent. **THE HEADER FORMAT IS REVIT'S, NOT A CONVENTION.** Each column reads `Name##type##unit` - "DN##length##millimeters" - and the first column is the key and is unnamed. A header Revit cannot parse is refused with the column and the text that failed, which is reported rather than swallowed: an import that quietly does nothing looks exactly like one that worked. **IT NEEDS THE FAMILY OPEN FOR EDITING.** A lookup table belongs to the family document. Run it with a project in front and it says so. **A FAMILY WITH NO TABLE MANAGER GETS ONE.** Importing into a family that never had a lookup table is a legitimate first import, so the manager is created rather than refused - and the answer says that is what happened, because gaining a table is a bigger change than gaining a row. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

| **You say** | **csv path** - text<br>**table name** - text |
| **You get** | imported, rows before, rows after, table created, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
